translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 203

sentences.zh: 卷第二百三

translations.literal: Volume CCIII
translations.idiomatic: Volume 203

sentences.zh: 【唐紀十九】　起玄黓敦牂，盡柔兆閹茂，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 19] Beginning in the year Xuanqu Dunzang and ending in the year Rouzhao Yanmao, five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 19] From the cyclical year Xuanqu Dunzang through Rouzhao Yanmao—a span of five years.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，作萬泉宮於藍田。

translations.literal: In spring, in the second month, the Wanquan Palace was built at Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: That spring, in the second month, construction of the Wanquan Palace began at Lantian.

sentences.zh: 癸未，改元，赦天下。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, the era name was changed and amnesty was granted throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day, the reign era was changed and a general amnesty was proclaimed empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 戊午，立皇孫重照為皇太孫。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, the imperial grandson Chongzhao was established as imperial grand-son.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day, the emperor's grandson Chongzhao was named imperial grand-son.

sentences.zh: 上欲令開府置僚屬，問吏部郎中王方慶，對曰：「晉及齊皆嘗立太孫，其太子官屬即為太孫官屬，未聞太子在東宮而更立太孫者也。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to have an office opened and staff appointed; he asked Wang Fangqing, a director in the Ministry of Personnel, who replied: "Both Jin and Qi once established an imperial grand-son; the crown prince's staff served as the grand-son's staff. One has not heard of establishing an imperial grand-son while the crown prince still resided in the Eastern Palace."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to open a household office and appoint staff for him. He consulted Wang Fangqing, a director in the Ministry of Personnel, who answered: "Jin and Qi had both installed an imperial grand-son, using the crown prince's staff as his staff. I know of no precedent for naming a grand-son while the crown prince still held court in the Eastern Palace."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「自我作古，可乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If I myself create the precedent, may I?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "If I establish the precedent myself, would that be permissible?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「三王不相襲禮，何為不可！

translations.literal: He replied: "The three sage kings did not inherit one another's rites—why should it not be possible!"
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing replied, "The three sage kings did not simply inherit one another's ritual codes—why should this be impossible?"

sentences.zh: 」乃奏置師傅等官。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized to establish tutors and other offices.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial proposing tutors and other offices.

sentences.zh: 既而上疑其非法，竟不補授。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor doubted that it was not lawful and in the end did not fill the appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor later doubted the arrangement's legality and ultimately never filled the posts.

sentences.zh: 方慶，裒之曾孫也，名綝，以字行。

translations.literal: Fangqing was a great-grandson of Bao; his personal name was Shen, but he was known by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing was a great-grandson of Wang Bao; his given name was Shen, but he went by his style name.

sentences.zh: 西突厥阿史那車簿帥十姓反。

translations.literal: Ashina Chebo of the Western Turks led the Ten Surnames in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Chebo of the Western Turks rallied the Ten Surnames in revolt.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the first day jiazi of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the first day of the fourth month (jiazi), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 上以關中饑饉，米斗三百，將幸東都；

translations.literal: Because of famine in Guanzhong, with rice at three hundred cash per dou, the emperor was about to proceed to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped Guanzhong, and rice reached three hundred cash per dou, so the emperor prepared to travel to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，發京師，留太子監國，使劉仁軌、裴炎、薛元超輔之。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin he departed the capital, leaving the crown prince to oversee the state and appointing Liu Ren'gui, Pei Yan, and Xue Yuanchao to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day he left the capital, leaving the crown prince as regent with Liu Ren'gui, Pei Yan, and Xue Yuanchao to advise him.

sentences.zh: 時出幸倉猝，扈從之士有餓死於中道者。

translations.literal: The journey was made in haste; among the followers some starved to death on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The departure had been so sudden that some in the imperial escort starved to death along the way.

sentences.zh: 上慮道路多草竊，使監察御史魏元忠檢校車駕前後。

translations.literal: The emperor feared many bandits along the route and sent the investigating censor Wei Yuanzhong to inspect before and behind the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing bandits along the route, the emperor charged investigating censor Wei Yuanzhong with securing the procession.

sentences.zh: 元忠受詔，即閱視赤縣獄，得盜一人，神采語言異於眾，命釋桎梏，襲冠帶，乘驛以從，與之共食宿，托以詰盜，其人笑許諾。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong received the edict, immediately reviewed the metropolitan county prisons, and found one thief whose bearing and speech differed from the rest; he ordered his fetters removed, gave him cap and belt, had him ride post-horses in attendance, shared food and lodging with him, and entrusted him to interrogate bandits; the man smiled and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong took the order, inspected the capital county jails at once, and singled out one prisoner whose manner and speech set him apart. He had the man unshackled, dressed in cap and sash, and brought along on post horses; they ate and slept together while Yuanzhong enlisted him to hunt down robbers. The man laughed and accepted.

sentences.zh: 比及東都，士馬萬數，不亡一錢。

translations.literal: By the time they reached the Eastern Capital, among tens of thousands of soldiers and horses, not a single coin was lost.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached the Eastern Capital, not one coin was lost among the tens of thousands of men and horses.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以禮部尚書聞喜憲公裴行儉為金牙道行軍大總管，帥右金吾將軍閻懷旦等三總管分道討西突厥。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Pei Xingjian, Duke Xian of Wenxi, Minister of Rites, was made Grand Commander of the Jinya Route campaign army, leading three commanders including the Right Golden Guard General Yan Huaidan in separate columns to attack the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day, Pei Xingjian, Duke Xian of Wenxi and Minister of Rites, was appointed grand commander of the Jinya Route army, with Right Golden Guard General Yan Huaidan and two other commanders to strike the Western Turks by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 師未行，行儉薨。

translations.literal: Before the army marched, Xingjian died.
translations.idiomatic: Before the troops could march, Xingjian died.

sentences.zh: 行儉有知人之鑒，初為吏部侍郎，前進士王劇、咸陽尉欒城蘇味道皆未知名。

translations.literal: Xingjian had a discerning eye for men. When he was first Vice Minister of Personnel, the former jinshi Wang Ju and Su Weidao, magistrate of Xianyang in Luancheng, were both still unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian was celebrated for judging character. Early in his tenure as vice minister of personnel, the former jinshi Wang Ju and Su Weidao of Luancheng, magistrate of Xianyang, were still obscure.

sentences.zh: 行儉一見，謂之曰：「二君後當相次常銓衡，僕有弱息，願以為托。

translations.literal: At one meeting Xingjian said to them: "You two will in turn hold the regular selection offices; I have a young daughter and wish to entrust her to you."
translations.idiomatic: At their first meeting he told them, "You will each in turn oversee the regular personnel selection. I have a young daughter and would like to entrust her to you."

sentences.zh: 」是時劇弟勃與華陰楊炯、范陽盧照鄰、義烏駱賓王皆以文章有盛名，司列少常伯李敬玄尤重之，以為必顯達。

translations.literal: At that time Ju's younger brother Bo, together with Yang Jiong of Huayin, Lu Zhaolin of Fanyang, and Luo Binwang of Yiwu, were all famed for literary talent; Li Jingxuan, Vice Director of the Secretariat, especially valued them and believed they would surely rise to eminence.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Ju's younger brother Bo, together with Yang Jiong of Huayin, Lu Zhaolin of Fanyang, and Luo Binwang of Yiwu, were famed for their writing. Li Jingxuan, vice director of the Secretariat, prized them highly and was certain they would rise.

sentences.zh: 行儉曰：「士之致遠者，當先器識而後才藝。

translations.literal: Xingjian said: "For a gentleman to go far, character and insight must come before literary skill."
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian said, "Men who go far put character and judgment ahead of literary talent."

sentences.zh: 勃等雖有文華，而浮躁淺露，豈享爵祿之器邪！

translations.literal: Although Bo and the others have literary brilliance, they are restless and shallow—how could they be vessels fit to enjoy rank and stipend!"
translations.idiomatic: "Bo and his circle may be brilliant writers, but they are flighty and shallow. Are they fit to hold high office and emoluments?"

sentences.zh: 楊子稍沈靜，應至令長；

translations.literal: Young Yang is somewhat more composed and should reach the rank of district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: "Young Yang is somewhat steadier and may reach a magistracy."

sentences.zh: 餘得令終幸矣。

translations.literal: The rest would be fortunate to end their lives peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: "The rest would be lucky to die in bed."

sentences.zh: 」既而勃渡海墮水，炯終於盈川令，照鄰惡疾不愈，赴水死，賓王反誅，劇、味道皆典選，如行儉言。

translations.literal: Thereafter Bo drowned crossing the sea; Jiong ended his days as magistrate of Yingchuan; Zhaolin's chronic illness did not heal and he drowned himself; Binwang was executed for rebellion; Ju and Weidao both held selection offices, just as Xingjian had said.
translations.idiomatic: Events bore him out: Bo drowned at sea; Jiong died as magistrate of Yingchuan; Zhaolin's lingering illness drove him to drown himself; Binwang was executed for rebellion; Ju and Weidao each headed personnel selection, exactly as Xingjian had foretold.

sentences.zh: 行儉為將帥，所引偏裨如程務挺、張虔勖、王方翼、劉敬同、李多祚、黑齒常之，後多為名將。

translations.literal: As a commander, the subordinate officers he advanced—such as Cheng Wuting, Zhang Qianxu, Wang Fangyi, Liu Jingtong, Li Duozuo, and Heichi Changzhi—later mostly became famous generals.
translations.idiomatic: As a general he promoted subordinates such as Cheng Wuting, Zhang Qianxu, Wang Fangyi, Liu Jingtong, Li Duozuo, and Heichi Changzhi, most of whom later became celebrated commanders.

sentences.zh: 行儉嘗命左右取犀角、麝香而失之。

translations.literal: Xingjian once ordered his attendants to fetch rhinoceros horn and musk, and they were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xingjian sent attendants for rhinoceros horn and musk, and the items went missing.

sentences.zh: 又敕賜馬及鞍，令史輒馳驟，馬倒，鞍破。

translations.literal: Again an edict bestowed a horse and saddle; the clerk galloped off at once, the horse fell, and the saddle was broken.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion an edict granted him a horse and saddle; the clerk galloped away at once, the horse fell, and the saddle was ruined.

sentences.zh: 二人皆逃去，行儉使人召還，謂曰：「爾曹皆誤耳，何相輕之甚邪！

translations.literal: Both men fled; Xingjian sent for them to return and said: "You have all merely made mistakes—why take yourselves so lightly!"
translations.idiomatic: Both men fled, but Xingjian had them brought back and said, "These were only mistakes—why punish yourselves so harshly?"

sentences.zh: 」待之如故。

translations.literal: He treated them as before.
translations.idiomatic: He treated them as before.

sentences.zh: 破阿史那都支，得馬腦盤，廣二尺餘，以示將士，軍吏王休烈捧盤升階，跌而碎之，惶恐，叩頭流血。

translations.literal: After defeating Ashina Duzhi he obtained an agate tray more than two feet wide and showed it to the officers and soldiers; the army clerk Wang Xiulie bore the tray up the steps, stumbled, and shattered it; in terror he knocked his head until it bled.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Ashina Duzhi he seized an agate tray over two feet across and displayed it to the troops. Army clerk Wang Xiulie carried it up the steps, tripped, and smashed it; terrified, he knocked his head on the ground until it bled.

sentences.zh: 行儉笑曰：「爾非故為，何至於是！

translations.literal: Xingjian laughed and said: "You did not do it on purpose—why go to such lengths!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian laughed and said, "You did not do it on purpose—why take it so hard?"

sentences.zh: 」不復有追惜之色。

translations.literal: He showed no further regret.
translations.idiomatic: He showed no further regret.

sentences.zh: 詔賜都支等資產金器三千餘物，雜畜稱是，並分給親故及偏裨，數日而盡。

translations.literal: By edict he was granted more than three thousand items of property and gold vessels from Duzhi and the like, with livestock in proportion, all distributed to kin, friends, and subordinate officers within a few days.
translations.idiomatic: An edict awarded him more than three thousand pieces of booty and gold vessels from Duzhi's estate, along with a comparable herd of livestock, all of which he distributed to kin, friends, and subordinates within days.

sentences.zh: 阿史那車薄圍弓月城，安西都護王方翼引軍救之，破虜眾於伊麗水，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: Ashina Chebo besieged Gongyue City; Protector-General of Anxi Wang Fangyi led troops to relieve it, defeated the enemy host on the Yili River, and took more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Chebo besieged Gongyue City. Wang Fangyi, protector-general of Anxi, marched to its relief, routed the enemy on the Yili River, and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 俄而三姓咽面與車薄合兵拒方翼，方翼與戰於熱海，流矢貫方翼臂，方翼以佩刀截之，左右不知。

translations.literal: Soon the Three Surnames Yanmian joined Chebo to oppose Fangyi; Fangyi fought them at Hot Sea; a stray arrow pierced his arm and he cut it off with his belt dagger—those around him did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Three Surnames Yanmian allied with Chebo against Fangyi. At Hot Sea a stray arrow pierced his arm; he severed the shaft with his dagger, and those around him never knew.

sentences.zh: 所將胡兵謀執方翼以應車薄，方翼知之，悉召會議，陽出軍資賜之，以次引出斬之，會大風，方翼振金鼓以亂其聲，誅七十餘人，其徒莫之覺。

translations.literal: The Hu soldiers he led plotted to seize Fangyi to join Chebo; Fangyi learned of it, summoned them all to council, pretended to issue army supplies as rewards, led them out one by one and beheaded them; when a great wind arose Fangyi beat gongs and drums to drown the sound—more than seventy were executed and their comrades did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his Hu troops plotted to seize him for Chebo. Fangyi learned of it, called a full council, pretended to distribute supplies as rewards, and had the conspirators led out one by one and beheaded. When a gale rose he beat drums and gongs to mask the noise; more than seventy were killed without the rest realizing.

sentences.zh: 既而分遣裨將襲車薄、咽面，大破之，擒其酋長三百人，西突厥遂平。

translations.literal: He then sent subordinate generals in separate attacks on Chebo and Yanmian, inflicted a great defeat, captured three hundred of their chieftains, and the Western Turks were thus pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent subordinates against Chebo and Yanmian, crushing them and capturing three hundred chieftains, and the Western Turks were pacified.

sentences.zh: 閻懷旦等竟不行。

translations.literal: Yan Huaidan and the others in the end did not march.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Huaidan and the others never marched at all.

sentences.zh: 方翼尋遷夏州都督，征入，議邊事。

translations.literal: Fangyi was soon transferred to be military commissioner of Xia Prefecture, summoned to court, and consulted on frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyi was soon made military commissioner of Xia Prefecture, recalled to court, and consulted on frontier policy.

sentences.zh: 上見方翼衣有血漬，問之，方翼具對熱海苦戰之狀，上視瘡歎息；

translations.literal: The emperor saw blood stains on Fangyi's clothing and asked; Fangyi gave a full account of the bitter fighting at Hot Sea; the emperor looked at the wound and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noticed blood on Fangyi's clothes and asked why. Fangyi described the fierce fighting at Hot Sea in detail; the emperor examined the wound and sighed.

sentences.zh: 竟以廢後近屬，不得用而歸。

translations.literal: In the end, because he was a close kinsman of the deposed empress, he was not employed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, because he was kin to the deposed empress, he was passed over for appointment and sent home.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，車駕至東都。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou the imperial carriage arrived at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day the emperor reached the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以黃門侍郎穎川郭待舉、兵部侍郎岑長倩、秘書員外少監、檢校中書侍郎鼓城郭正一、吏部侍郎鼓城魏玄同並與中書門下同承受進止平章事。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, Guo Daiju of Yingchuan, Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate; Cen Changqian, Vice Minister of War; Guo Zhengyi of Gucheng, Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat and Acting Vice Minister of the Secretariat; and Wei Xuantong of Gucheng, Vice Minister of Personnel, were all made Associates of the Secretariat and Chancellery with the title of "Coordinator of Affairs."
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day, Guo Daiju of Yingchuan (vice minister of the yellow gate), Cen Changqian (vice minister of war), Guo Zhengyi of Gucheng (acting vice director of the secretariat), and Wei Xuantong of Gucheng (vice minister of personnel) were all made associates of the Secretariat and Chancellery with the title Coordinator of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上欲用待舉等，謂崔知溫曰：「待舉等資任尚淺，且令預聞政事，未可與卿等同名。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to employ Daiju and the others and said to Cui Zhiwen: "Daiju and the others are still shallow in seniority and experience; for now let them participate in hearing state affairs—they may not yet share your title."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to use Daiju and his colleagues and told Cui Zhiwen, "Their seniority is still modest; let them sit in on state affairs for now, but they may not yet share your formal title."

sentences.zh: 」自是外司四品已下知政事者，始以平章事為名。

translations.literal: From this time, those outside the inner secretariat of fourth rank and below who participated in government affairs first bore the name "Coordinator of Affairs."
translations.idiomatic: From then on, officials outside the inner secretariat of fourth rank or below who shared in governance were first called Coordinators of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 長倩，文本之兄子也。

translations.literal: Changqian was a nephew of Cen Text.
translations.idiomatic: Changqian was a nephew of Cen Text.

sentences.zh: 先是，玄同為吏部侍郎，上言銓選之弊，以為：「人君之體，當委任而責成功，所委者當，則所用者自精矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xuantong was Vice Minister of Personnel, he memorialized on the abuses of selection, holding that: "The proper stance of a ruler is to delegate responsibility and demand results; if those delegated are right, those employed will of themselves be refined."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as vice minister of personnel, Xuantong had memorialized on abuses in appointment, arguing that a ruler should delegate authority and hold men accountable for results; if the delegates were sound, the appointees would be sound as well.

sentences.zh: 故周穆王命伯冏為太僕正，曰：『慎簡乃僚。

translations.literal: Therefore King Mu of Zhou appointed Bo Jiong Grand Master of Servants and said: "Carefully choose your subordinates."
translations.idiomatic: King Mu of Zhou appointed Bo Jiong grand master of servants with the charge, "Choose your subordinates with care."

sentences.zh: 』是使群司各自求其小者，而天子命其大者也。

translations.literal: This was to have each office seek its own lesser men while the Son of Heaven appointed the greater ones.
translations.idiomatic: Each ministry was to find its own junior staff while the Son of Heaven named the senior ones.

sentences.zh: 乃至漢氏，得人皆自州縣補署，五府辟召，然後升於天朝，自魏、晉以來，始專委選部。

translations.literal: Down to the Han, worthy men were all appointed from prefecture and county posts, summoned by the Five Offices, and only then promoted to the imperial court; from Wei and Jin onward, appointment was entrusted solely to the Selection Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, men rose from county and prefectural posts, were recruited by the five offices, and only then advanced to court. From Wei and Jin onward, selection was concentrated in the personnel bureau alone.

sentences.zh: 夫以天下之大，士人之眾，而委之數人之手，用刀筆以量才，按簿書而察行，借使平如權衡，明如水鏡，猶力有所極，照有所窮，況所委非人而有愚闇阿私之弊乎！

translations.literal: To entrust the vast realm and multitude of scholars to the hands of a few men, measuring talent with the brush and examining conduct by ledger—even if level as scales and clear as a water mirror, still strength has its limit and illumination its bounds, how much more when those entrusted are unworthy and there are the abuses of folly, obscurity, and favoritism!
translations.idiomatic: To leave the vast empire and its legions of scholars to a handful of clerks, gauging talent with paperwork and character from registers—even the fairest scales and clearest mirror have limits. How much worse when the delegates are unfit, breeding stupidity, favoritism, and corruption!

sentences.zh: 願略依周、漢之規以救魏、晉之失。

translations.literal: I wish to follow in outline the regulations of Zhou and Han to remedy the errors of Wei and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that we restore in outline the Zhou and Han systems to correct the Wei and Jin mistake.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but not adopted.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙午，東都霖雨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day bingwu, there was prolonged rain in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingwu day, the Eastern Capital was lashed by unending rain.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，洛水溢，溺民居千餘家。

translations.literal: On the day yimao the Luo River overflowed and drowned more than a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day the Luo River burst its banks and drowned more than a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 關中先水後旱、蝗，繼以疾疫，米斗四百，兩京間死者相枕於路，人相食。

translations.literal: In Guanzhong there was first flood, then drought and locusts, followed by pestilence; rice was four hundred cash per dou; between the two capitals the dead lay pillow to pillow on the roads and men ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong suffered flood, then drought and locusts, then plague; rice reached four hundred cash per dou. Between the two capitals corpses lined the roads, and people resorted to cannibalism.

sentences.zh: 上既封泰山，欲遍封五嶽，秋，七月，作奉天宮於嵩山南。

translations.literal: The emperor, having already performed the Feng sacrifice on Mount Tai, wished to perform the sacrifices on all Five Sacred Peaks; in autumn, in the seventh month, the Fengtian Palace was built south of Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: After his Feng sacrifice on Mount Tai, the emperor planned to enfeoff all five sacred peaks. That autumn, in the seventh month, work began on the Fengtian Palace south of Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 監察御史裡行李善感諫曰：「陛下封泰山，告太平，致群瑞，與三皇、五帝比隆矣。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Li Shangan remonstrated: "Your Majesty performed the Feng on Mount Tai, announced great peace, brought forth many auspicious signs, and may be compared in grandeur to the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors."
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Li Shangan remonstrated: "Your Majesty has offered the Feng on Mount Tai, proclaimed great peace, gathered auspicious omens, and may stand beside the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors in glory."

sentences.zh: 數年已來，菽粟不稔，餓殍相望，四夷交侵，兵車歲駕；

translations.literal: For several years grain and millet have not ripened; the starving lie in sight of one another; the four barbarians invade in turn and war chariots are dispatched every year.
translations.idiomatic: For years the harvests have failed; the starving lie within sight of one another; barbarians raid from every quarter and the war chariots roll out each year.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜恭默思道以禳災譴，乃更廣營宮室，勞役不休，天下莫不失望。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought in reverent silence to ponder the Way to avert calamity and reproof; yet you further expand palaces and ceaseless corvée—the realm is everywhere disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should ponder the Way in reverent silence to avert Heaven's wrath, yet you expand palaces and press labor without rest. The empire is everywhere disheartened.

sentences.zh: 臣忝備國家耳目，竊以此為憂！

translations.literal: Your servant, unworthy to serve as the state's eyes and ears, privately takes this as a source of anxiety!
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy to serve as the state's eyes and ears, yet I cannot keep this grief to myself!

sentences.zh: 」上雖不納，亦優容之。

translations.literal: Although the emperor did not adopt it, he treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept the advice but received it graciously.

sentences.zh: 自褚遂良、韓瑗之死，中外以言為諱，無敢逆意直諫，幾二十年；

translations.literal: Since the deaths of Chu Suiliang and Han Yuan, within and without the court speech had become taboo and none dared to oppose the will with straight remonstrance—for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Since the deaths of Chu Suiliang and Han Yuan, frank speech had been taboo at court and beyond for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 及善感始諫，天下皆喜，謂之「鳳鳴朝陽」。

translations.literal: When Shangan first remonstrated, the realm rejoiced and called it "the phoenix crying at dawn."
translations.idiomatic: When Shangan spoke out, the realm rejoiced and called it "the phoenix crying at dawn."

sentences.zh: 上遣宦者緣江徙異竹，欲植苑中。

translations.literal: The emperor sent eunuchs along the river to transplant exotic bamboo, intending to plant it in the imperial park.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent eunuchs up the Yangtze to transplant exotic bamboo for the imperial gardens.

sentences.zh: 宦者科舟載竹，所在縱暴；

translations.literal: The eunuchs requisitioned boats to carry the bamboo and everywhere committed outrages.
translations.idiomatic: They commandeered boats to haul the bamboo and abused the populace wherever they passed.

sentences.zh: 過荊州，荊州長史蘇良嗣囚之，上疏切諫，以為：「致遠方異物，煩擾道路，恐非聖人愛人之意。

translations.literal: Passing through Jing Prefecture, the prefectural secretary Su Liangsi imprisoned them and submitted a sharp memorial, holding that: "Bringing exotic things from distant regions and troubling the roads is perhaps not the intent of a sage who loves the people."
translations.idiomatic: At Jing Prefecture the secretary Su Liangsi imprisoned them and submitted a sharp memorial: "Hauling exotic plants from afar and harassing the highways hardly accords with a sage ruler's care for his people."

sentences.zh: 又，小人竊弄威福，虧損皇明。

translations.literal: Moreover, petty men usurp authority and emolument, diminishing the imperial radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, petty men have usurped power and profit, tarnishing Your Majesty's glory.

sentences.zh: 」上謂天後曰：「吾約束不嚴，果為良嗣所怪。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the Heavenly Empress: "My discipline was not strict enough—I have indeed been reproved by Liangsi."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the empress, "I was not strict enough, and Liangsi has rightly called me to account."

sentences.zh: 」手詔慰諭良嗣，令棄竹江中。

translations.literal: He issued a personal edict to comfort and instruct Liangsi and ordered the bamboo cast into the river.
translations.idiomatic: He issued a personal edict praising Liangsi and ordered the bamboo dumped into the river.

sentences.zh: 良嗣，世長之子也。

translations.literal: Liangsi was a son of Shichang.
translations.idiomatic: Liangsi was a son of Su Shichang.

sentences.zh: 黔州都督謝祐希天後意，逼零陵王明令自殺，上深惜之，黔府官屬皆坐免官。

translations.literal: Xie You, military commissioner of Qian Prefecture, currying favor with the Heavenly Empress, forced Prince Ming of Lingling to take his own life; the emperor deeply regretted it and all Qian Prefecture officials were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xie You, military commissioner of Qian Prefecture, currying favor with the empress, forced Prince Ming of Lingling to commit suicide. The emperor deeply mourned him, and every Qian official was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 祐後寢於平閣，與婢妾十餘人共處，夜，失其首。

translations.literal: Later You slept in a pavilion, sharing quarters with more than ten maids and concubines; in the night his head was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Later You slept in a pavilion with a dozen maids and concubines; in the night his head vanished.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，明子零陵王俊、黎國公傑為天後所殺，有司籍其家，得祐首，漆為穢器，題雲謝祐，乃知明子使刺客取之也。

translations.literal: In the Chuigong era, Ming's sons Jun, Prince of Lingling, and Jie, Duke of Li, were killed by the Heavenly Empress; when officials inventoried their households they found You's head lacquered as a foul vessel inscribed "Xie You"—thus it was known that Ming's sons had sent assassins to take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chuigong era the empress executed Ming's sons Jun of Lingling and Jie of Li. When their estates were inventoried, You's head turned up lacquered as a latrine bucket labeled "Xie You"—proof that Ming's sons had sent assassins for it.

sentences.zh: 太子留守京師，頗事游畋，薛元超上疏規諫；

translations.literal: The crown prince, remaining at the capital, devoted himself much to hunting; Xue Yuanchao submitted a memorial of admonition.
translations.idiomatic: While the crown prince remained at the capital he devoted himself to hunting. Xue Yuanchao submitted a memorial of admonition.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，遣使者慰勞元超，仍召赴東都。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he sent an envoy to comfort and reward Yuanchao and also summoned him to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of it the emperor sent an envoy to commend Yuanchao and summoned him to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃將論欽陵寇柘、松、翼等州。

translations.literal: The Tibetan general Lun Qinling raided the prefectures of Zhe, Song, Yi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan general Lun Qinling raided Zhe, Song, Yi, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 詔左驍衛郎將李孝逸、右衛郎將衛蒲山發秦、渭等州兵分道御之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Li Xiaoyi, commandant of the Left Valiant Cavalry, and Wei Pushan, commandant of the Right Guard, to raise troops from Qin, Wei, and other prefectures in separate columns to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaoyi of the Left Valiant Cavalry and Wei Pushan of the Right Guard were ordered to raise troops from Qin, Wei, and other prefectures and meet the invasion on separate routes.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙寅，黃門侍郎劉景先同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day bingyin, Liu Jingxian, Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate, was made Associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery with the title Coordinator of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on bingyin day, Liu Jingxian, vice minister of the yellow gate, was made coordinator of affairs at the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 是歲，突厥餘黨阿史那骨篤祿、阿史德元珍等招集亡散，據黑沙城反，入寇并州及單于府之北境，殺嵐州刺史王德茂。

translations.literal: That year the Turk remnant Ashina Gudulu, Ashide Yuanzhen, and others gathered the scattered and lost, seized Heisha City in rebellion, invaded Bing Prefecture and the northern border of the Chanyu Protectorate, and killed Wang Demao, prefect of Lan.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Turk remnant leaders Ashina Gudulu and Ashide Yuanzhen rallied scattered followers, seized Heisha City, raided Bing Prefecture and the northern Chanyu Protectorate, and killed Wang Demao, prefect of Lan.

sentences.zh: 右領軍衛將軍、檢校代州都督薛仁貴將兵擊元珍於雲州，虜問唐大將為誰，應之曰：「薛仁貴！

translations.literal: Xue Rengui, general of the Right Army Guard and acting military commissioner of Dai Prefecture, led troops to strike Yuanzhen at Yun Prefecture; the barbarians asked who was the Tang great general and were answered: "Xue Rengui!"
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rengui, general of the Right Army Guard and acting commissioner of Dai Prefecture, attacked Yuanzhen at Yun Prefecture. The enemy asked who commanded the Tang army and were told, "Xue Rengui!"

sentences.zh: 」虜曰：「吾聞仁貴流象州，死久矣，何以紿我！

translations.literal: The barbarians said: "We heard Rengui was exiled to Xiang Prefecture and died long ago—why deceive us!"
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "We heard Rengui was exiled to Xiang Prefecture and died long ago. Why try to fool us?"

sentences.zh: 仁貴免冑示之面，虜相顧失色，下馬列拜，稍稍引去。

translations.literal: Rengui removed his helmet and showed his face; the barbarians looked at one another and turned pale, dismounted and lined up to bow, and gradually withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui removed his helmet and showed his face. The enemy stared, turned pale, dismounted in ranks to bow, and slowly withdrew.

sentences.zh: 仁貴因奮擊，大破之，斬首萬餘級，捕虜二萬餘人。

translations.literal: Rengui then pressed the attack and inflicted a great defeat, taking more than ten thousand heads and capturing more than twenty thousand prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui pressed the attack, routing them with more than ten thousand heads taken and twenty thousand prisoners captured.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃入寇河源軍，軍使婁師德將兵擊之於白水澗，八戰八捷。

translations.literal: The Tibetans invaded Heyuan Army; army commissioner Lou Shide led troops to strike them at Baishui Ravine and won eight battles in eight engagements.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetans raided Heyuan Army. Commissioner Lou Shide met them at Baishui Ravine and won eight battles in eight engagements.

sentences.zh: 上以師德為比部員外郎、左驍衛郎將、河源軍經略副使，曰：「卿有文武材，勿辭也！

translations.literal: The emperor made Shide an outer-office director in the Ministry of Justice, commandant of the Left Valiant Cavalry, and deputy commissioner for Heyuan Army, saying: "You have both civil and military talent—do not decline!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Shide outer-office director in the Ministry of Justice, commandant of the Left Valiant Cavalry, and deputy commissioner of Heyuan Army, saying, "You have both civil and military talent—do not refuse!"

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲午朔，上行幸奉天宮。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on the first day jiawu of the month, the emperor proceeded to the Fengtian Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That spring, on the first day of the first month (jiawu), the emperor traveled to the Fengtian Palace.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚午，突厥寇定州，刺史霍王元軌擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day gengwu, the Turks raided Ding Prefecture; the prefect, Prince Yuangui of Huo, repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengwu day, Turks raided Ding Prefecture; Prince Yuangui of Huo, the prefect, drove them off.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，復寇媯州。

translations.literal: On the day yihai they again raided Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day they raided Ji Prefecture again.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚寅，阿史那骨篤祿、阿史德元珍圍單于都護府，執司馬張行師，殺之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day gengyin, Ashina Gudulu and Ashide Yuanzhen besieged the Chanyu Protectorate, seized the aide Zhang Xingshi, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengyin day, Gudulu and Yuanzhen besieged the Chanyu Protectorate, seized aide Zhang Xingshi, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 遣勝州都督王本立、夏州都督李崇義將兵分道救之。

translations.literal: Wang Benli, military commissioner of Sheng Prefecture, and Li Chongyi, military commissioner of Xia Prefecture, were sent with troops in separate columns to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Benli of Sheng Prefecture and Li Chongyi of Xia Prefecture were dispatched with troops on separate routes to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 太子右庶子、同中書門下三品李義琰改葬父母，使其舅氏遷舊墓；

translations.literal: Li Yiyan, Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household and Associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the third rank, reburied his parents and had his maternal uncle move the old graves.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yiyan, right vice director of the crown prince's household and third-rank associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery, reburied his parents and had his maternal uncle relocate the old graves.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，怒曰：「義琰倚勢，乃陵其舅家，不可復知政事！

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he said in anger: "Yiyan relies on his power and bullies his uncle's family—he may no longer participate in government affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he flew into a rage: "Yiyan is abusing his position to bully his uncle's household. He must never again take part in government!"

sentences.zh: 」義琰聞之，不自安，以足疾乞骸骨。

translations.literal: When Yiyan heard of it he was ill at ease and, citing foot ailment, requested to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyan, uneasy at the reprimand, pleaded foot ailment and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以義琰為銀青光祿大夫，致仕。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi he made Yiyan Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and granted him retirement.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Yiyan was made Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and permitted to retire.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，守中書令崔知溫薨。

translations.literal: On the day guichou Cui Zhiwen, acting Director of the Secretariat, died.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day Cui Zhiwen, acting director of the Secretariat, died.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己未，車駕還東都。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day jiwei, the imperial carriage returned to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, in the fourth month, on jiwei day, the emperor returned to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 綏州步落稽白鐵余，埋銅佛於地中，久之，草生其上，紿其鄉人曰：「吾於此數見佛光。

translations.literal: Bai Tiesu of the Buluoji tribe in Sui Prefecture buried a bronze Buddha in the ground; after a long time grass grew above it, and he deceived his fellow villagers, saying: "I have several times seen Buddha-light here."
translations.idiomatic: Bai Tiesu, a Buluoji tribesman of Sui Prefecture, buried a bronze Buddha in the earth. Grass eventually grew over the spot, and he told his neighbors, "I have often seen a Buddha-light here."

sentences.zh: 」擇日集眾掘地，果得之，因曰：「得見聖佛者，百疾皆愈。

translations.literal: On a chosen day he gathered the multitude to dig, and indeed obtained it; he then said: "Whoever beholds the holy Buddha—all hundred ailments are cured."
translations.idiomatic: On a chosen day he gathered a crowd to dig, and the image was found. He declared, "Whoever sees this holy Buddha will be cured of every illness."

sentences.zh: 」遠近赴之。

translations.literal: People came from far and near.
translations.idiomatic: People flocked from far and near.

sentences.zh: 鐵余以雜色囊盛之數十重，得厚施，乃去一囊。

translations.literal: Tiesu wrapped it in dozens of layers of colored bags, received generous offerings, and then removed one bag.
translations.idiomatic: Tiesu wrapped the statue in dozens of colored sacks, collected lavish offerings, then removed one layer of wrapping.

sentences.zh: 數年間，歸信者眾，遂謀作亂。

translations.literal: Within several years believers were many, and he then plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years his following swelled, and he plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 據城平縣，自稱光明聖皇帝，置百官，進攻綏德、大斌二縣，殺官吏，焚民居。

translations.literal: He seized Ping County, styled himself Bright Sacred Emperor, established a full bureaucracy, and attacked the counties of Suide and Dabin, killing officials and burning dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Ping County, proclaimed himself Bright Sacred Emperor, appointed officials, and attacked Suide and Dabin, killing magistrates and burning homes.

sentences.zh: 遣右武衛將軍程務挺與夏州都督王方翼討之，甲申，攻拔其城，擒鐵余，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: The Right Martial Guard General Cheng Wuting and Xia Prefecture Commissioner Wang Fangyi were sent to suppress them; on the day jiashen they stormed the city, captured Tiesu, and all remaining rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wuting of the Right Martial Guard and Wang Fangyi, commissioner of Xia Prefecture, were dispatched against him. On jiashen day they stormed the city, captured Tiesu, and pacified the remnant rebels.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚寅，上幸芳桂宮，至合璧宮，遇大雨而還。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day gengyin, the emperor visited Fragrant Cassia Palace, reached United Jade Palace, encountered heavy rain, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengyin day, the emperor visited Fragrant Cassia Palace and reached United Jade Palace, but heavy rain forced him back.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，突厥阿史那骨篤祿等寇蔚州，殺刺史李思儉，豐州都督崔智辯將兵邀之於朝那山北，兵敗，為虜所擒。

translations.literal: On the day yisi the Turks Ashina Gudulu and others raided Wei Prefecture and killed Prefect Li Sijian; Feng Prefecture Commissioner Cui Zhibian led troops to intercept them north of Chaona Mountain, was defeated, and was captured by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day Gudulu and other Turks raided Wei Prefecture and killed Prefect Li Sijian. Cui Zhibian of Feng Prefecture intercepted them north of Chaona Mountain, was defeated, and taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲廢豐州，遷其百姓於靈、夏。

translations.literal: Court discussion wished to abolish Feng Prefecture and relocate its people to Ling and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated abolishing Feng Prefecture and resettling its people in Ling and Xia.

sentences.zh: 豐州司馬唐休璟上言，以為：「豐州阻河為固，居賊衝要，自秦、漢已來，列為郡縣，土宜耕牧。

translations.literal: Tang Xiujing, aide of Feng Prefecture, memorialized, holding that: "Feng Prefecture is fortified by the river and sits on a vital barbarian route; since Qin and Han it has been a commandery and county, its soil fit for farming and grazing."
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xiujing, aide of Feng Prefecture, argued that Feng was fortified by the Yellow River, lay on a critical frontier route, and had been a regular prefecture since Qin and Han—its land was ideal for farming and grazing.

sentences.zh: 隋季喪亂，遷百姓於寧、慶二州，致胡虜深侵，以靈、夏為邊境。

translations.literal: In the disorders at the end of Sui the people were moved to Ning and Qing prefectures, causing deep barbarian incursion and making Ling and Xia the border.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui collapse its people were moved to Ning and Qing, inviting deeper barbarian raids and pushing the border back to Ling and Xia.

sentences.zh: 貞觀之末，募人實之，西北始安。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguan settlers were recruited to fill it and the northwest was first pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhenguan era colonists were recruited to repopulate it, and the northwest was finally secured.

sentences.zh: 今廢之則河濱之地復為賊有，靈、夏等州人不安業，非國家之利也！

translations.literal: If it is now abolished the lands along the river will again fall to the enemy, and the people of Ling, Xia, and other prefectures will be unable to settle in their occupations—this is not to the state's advantage!
translations.idiomatic: To abandon it now would hand the riverlands back to the enemy and unsettle Ling, Xia, and neighboring prefectures. That would not serve the state!

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: The plan was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 六月，突厥別部寇掠嵐州，偏將楊玄基擊走之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month a separate Turk division raided Lan Prefecture; the subordinate general Yang Xuanji repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month a Turk splinter force raided Lan Prefecture; subordinate general Yang Xuanji drove them off.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己丑，立皇孫重福為唐昌王。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day jichou, the imperial grandson Chongfu was established as Prince of Tangchang.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, in the seventh month, on jichou day, the imperial grandson Chongfu was created Prince of Tangchang.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，詔以今年十月有事於嵩山；

translations.literal: On the day gengchen an edict ordered the rites on Mount Song for the tenth month of this year.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day an edict scheduled the Mount Song rites for the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 尋以上不豫，改用來年正月。

translations.literal: Soon because the emperor was unwell it was changed to the first month of the coming year.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's illness soon forced a postponement to the first month of the following year.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，徙相王輪為豫王，更名旦。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen the Prince of Xiang, Lun, was moved to be Prince of Yu and renamed Dan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Prince Lun of Xiang was made Prince of Yu and renamed Dan.

sentences.zh: 中書令兼太子左庶子薛元超病喑，乞骸骨；

translations.literal: Xue Yuanchao, Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household, fell ill with loss of voice and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yuanchao, director of the Secretariat and left vice director of the crown prince's household, lost his voice to illness and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 八月，己丑，以將封嵩山，召太子赴東都；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day jichou, because the Mount Song enfeoffment was imminent, the crown prince was summoned to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jichou day, with the Mount Song rites approaching, the crown prince was summoned to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 留唐昌王重福守京師，以劉仁軌為之副。

translations.literal: Prince Chongfu of Tangchang was left to guard the capital, with Liu Ren'gui as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chongfu of Tangchang was left to guard the capital, with Liu Ren'gui as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己卯，太子至東都。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day jimao, the crown prince reached the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on jimao day, the crown prince arrived at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，車駕幸奉天宮。

translations.literal: On the day guihai the imperial carriage visited the Fengtian Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day the emperor traveled to the Fengtian Palace.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙戌，詔罷來年封嵩山，上疾甚故也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day bingxu, an edict canceled the Mount Song rites for the coming year because the emperor's illness was severe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingxu day, an edict canceled next year's Mount Song rites because the emperor was gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 上苦頭重，不能視，召侍醫秦鳴鶴診之，鳴鶴請刺頭出血，可愈。

translations.literal: The emperor suffered heaviness in the head and could not see; he summoned the attending physician Qin Minghe to examine him; Minghe asked to prick the head to draw blood, saying he could be cured.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's head felt leaden and he could not see. He summoned the court physician Qin Minghe, who proposed bleeding the scalp and promised a cure.

sentences.zh: 天後在簾中，不欲上疾愈，怒曰：「此可斬也，乃欲於天子頭刺血！

translations.literal: The Heavenly Empress was behind the curtain and did not wish the emperor to recover; she said in anger: "This man deserves execution—he would prick blood from the Son of Heaven's head!"
translations.idiomatic: Behind the curtain the empress, who did not want him to recover, raged: "This man deserves death—he would draw blood from the Son of Heaven's head!"

sentences.zh: 」鳴鶴叩頭請命。

translations.literal: Minghe knocked his head and begged for his life.
translations.idiomatic: Minghe kowtowed and begged for his life.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「但刺之，未必不佳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Just prick it—it may not be a bad thing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Go ahead and prick—it may do no harm."

sentences.zh: 」乃刺百會、腦戶二穴。

translations.literal: He then pricked the two points Baihui and Naohu.
translations.idiomatic: He then bled the Baihui and Naohu points.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「吾目似明矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "My eyes seem clear now."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "My eyes seem clear now."

sentences.zh: 」後舉手加額曰：「天賜也！

translations.literal: Later he raised his hand to his forehead and said: "A gift from Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Later he pressed his hand to his brow and cried, "A gift from Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 」自負彩百匹以賜鳴鶴。

translations.literal: He personally carried a hundred bolts of colored silk to reward Minghe.
translations.idiomatic: He personally presented a hundred bolts of colored silk to reward Minghe.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以右武衛將軍程務挺為單于道安撫大使，招討阿史那骨篤祿等。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu Cheng Wuting, general of the Right Martial Guard, was made Pacification Commissioner of the Chanyu Route to recruit and suppress Ashina Gudulu and others.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day Cheng Wuting of the Right Martial Guard was made pacification commissioner of the Chanyu Route to subdue Gudulu and his followers.

sentences.zh: 詔太子監國，以裴炎、劉景先、郭正一兼東宮平章事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the crown prince to oversee the state; Pei Yan, Liu Jingxian, and Guo Zhengyi were made concurrent Eastern Palace Coordinators of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was ordered to act as regent, with Pei Yan, Liu Jingxian, and Guo Zhengyi as his coordinating ministers.

sentences.zh: 上自奉天宮疾甚，宰相皆不得見。

translations.literal: Since leaving the Fengtian Palace the emperor had been gravely ill and the chief ministers were all unable to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Since leaving the Fengtian Palace the emperor had been gravely ill, and the chief ministers could not gain audience.

sentences.zh: 丁未，還東都，百官見於天津橋南。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei he returned to the Eastern Capital; the hundred officials were received south of Tianjin Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day he returned to the Eastern Capital; officials were received south of Tianjin Bridge.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁巳，改元，赦天下。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day dingsi, the era name was changed and amnesty was granted throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingsi day, the reign era was changed and a general amnesty proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 上欲御則天門樓宣赦，氣逆不能乘馬，乃召百姓入殿前宣之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to ascend Zetian Gate tower to proclaim the amnesty but, with reversed qi, could not ride a horse; he therefore summoned the people before the hall to proclaim it.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to proclaim the amnesty from Zetian Gate tower but was too short of breath to ride; the proclamation was read instead before the palace hall to the assembled populace.

sentences.zh: 是夜，召裴炎入，受遺詔輔政，上崩於貞觀殿。

translations.literal: That night Pei Yan was summoned in to receive the testamentary edict as regent; the emperor died in the Zhenguan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That night Pei Yan was summoned to receive the deathbed edict appointing him regent. The emperor died in the Zhenguan Hall.

sentences.zh: 遺詔太子柩前即位，軍國大事有不決者，兼取天后進止。

translations.literal: The testament ordered the crown prince to ascend the throne before the coffin; on military and state matters that could not be decided, the Heavenly Empress's judgment was also to be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The testament directed the crown prince to ascend the throne before the bier. On military and civil matters that could not be resolved, the empress dowager's word was also to be sought.

sentences.zh: 廢萬泉、芳桂、奉天等宮。

translations.literal: The Wanquan, Fragrant Cassia, Fengtian, and other palaces were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Wanquan, Fragrant Cassia, Fengtian, and other pleasure palaces were abolished.

sentences.zh: 庚申，裴炎奏太子未即位，未應宣敕，有要速處分，望宣天後令於中書、門下施行。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen Pei Yan memorialized that the crown prince had not yet ascended the throne and edicts should not yet be proclaimed; on urgent matters he asked that the Heavenly Empress's orders be issued through the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day Pei Yan argued that with the crown prince not yet enthroned, no imperial edicts should issue; urgent business should be handled by edicts in the empress dowager's name through the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 甲子，中宗即位，尊天后為皇太后，政事鹹取決焉。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi Zhongzong ascended the throne and honored the Heavenly Empress as empress dowager; all government affairs were decided by her.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day Zhongzong ascended the throne and honored the late emperor's consort as empress dowager. All government decisions rested with her.

sentences.zh: 太后以澤州刺史韓王元嘉等，地尊望重，恐其為變，並加三公等官以慰其心。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, because Prince Yuangui of Han and others, as prefect of Ze and men of high standing and heavy prestige, might stir trouble, all added offices such as the Three Excellencies to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Prince Yuangui of Han and other senior princes of high prestige might plot trouble, the empress dowager showered them with honorary ranks such as the Three Excellencies to win their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以劉仁軌為左僕射，裴炎為中書令；

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu Liu Ren'gui was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Pei Yan Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day Liu Ren'gui was made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and Pei Yan director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以劉景先為侍中。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin Liu Jingxian was made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day Liu Jingxian was made attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 故事，宰相於門下省議事，謂之政事堂，故長孫無忌為司空，房玄齡為僕射，魏徵為太子太師，皆知門下省事。

translations.literal: By precedent the chief ministers deliberated at the Chancellery, called the Hall of Administration; thus when Zhangsun Wuji was Minister of Works, Fang Xuanling Vice Director, and Wei Zheng Grand Tutor of the Heir, all knew Chancellery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the chief ministers met in the Chancellery at the Hall of Administration. When Zhangsun Wuji was minister of works, Fang Xuanling vice director, and Wei Zheng grand tutor of the heir, all handled Chancellery business.

sentences.zh: 及裴炎遷中書令，始遷政事堂於中書省。

translations.literal: When Pei Yan was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, the Hall of Administration was first moved to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Yan became director of the Secretariat, the Hall of Administration was moved to the Secretariat for the first time.

sentences.zh: 壬午，遣左威衛將軍王果、左監門將軍令狐智通、右金吾將軍楊玄儉、右千牛將軍郭齊宗分往並、益、荊、揚四大都督府，與府司相知鎮守。

translations.literal: On the day renwu Wang Guo, general of the Left Majestic Guard; Linghu Zhitong, general of the Left Palace Gate; Yang Xuanjian, general of the Right Golden Guard; and Guo Qizong, general of the Right Millennial Ox, were sent in separate directions to the four great area commands of Bing, Yi, Jing, and Yang, to coordinate defense with the command staffs.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day Wang Guo of the Left Majestic Guard, Linghu Zhitong of the Left Palace Gate, Yang Xuanjian of the Right Golden Guard, and Guo Qizong of the Right Millennial Ox were dispatched to the Bing, Yi, Jing, and Yang area commands to coordinate defense with local staffs.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎同平章事郭正一為國子祭酒，罷政事。

translations.literal: Guo Zhengyi, Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Coordinator of Affairs, was made Rector of the National University and removed from government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhengyi, vice minister of the Secretariat and coordinator of affairs, was made rector of the National University and dismissed from the council.

sentences.zh: 則天順聖皇后上之上

translations.literal: Above: Empress Zetian Shunsheng
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu Zetian, Shunsheng — Part One

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲申朔，改元嗣聖，赦天下。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on the first day jiashen of the month, the era name was changed to Sisheng and amnesty was granted throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: That spring, on the first day of the first month (jiashen), the era was renamed Sisheng and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 立太子妃韋氏為皇后；

translations.literal: The crown prince's consort, the Lady Wei, was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's consort, Lady Wei, was made empress.

sentences.zh: 擢後父玄貞自普州參軍為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: The empress's father Xuanzhen was promoted from military aide in Pu Prefecture to prefect of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Wei Xuanzhen was promoted from a military aide post in Pu Prefecture to prefect of Yu.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以左散騎常侍杜陵韋弘敏為太府卿、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: On the day guisi Wei Hongmin of Duling, Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse, was made Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and Associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day Wei Hongmin of Duling, left regular attendant of the palace horse, was made director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and third-rank associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 中宗欲以韋玄貞為侍中，又欲授乳母之子五品官；

translations.literal: Zhongzong wished to make Wei Xuanzhen Attendant-in-Ordinary and also wished to grant the son of his wet nurse a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong wanted to make Wei Xuanzhen attendant-in-ordinary and to grant a fifth-rank office to his wet nurse's son.

sentences.zh: 裴炎固爭，中宗怒曰：「我以天下與韋玄貞，何不可！

translations.literal: Pei Yan firmly opposed it; Zhongzong said in anger: "I would give the realm to Wei Xuanzhen—why not!"
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yan objected firmly. Zhongzong raged, "I would give the empire to Wei Xuanzhen—why not?"

sentences.zh: 而惜侍中邪！

translations.literal: Yet you begrudge him Attendant-in-Ordinary!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet you begrudge him the post of attendant-in-ordinary!"

sentences.zh: 」炎懼，白太后，密謀廢立。

translations.literal: Yan feared this, informed the empress dowager, and secretly plotted deposition and enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yan, alarmed, informed the empress dowager and secretly plotted to depose him.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊午，太后集百官於乾元殿，裴炎與中書侍郎劉禕之、羽林將軍程務挺、張虔勖勒兵入宮，宣太后令，廢中宗為廬陵王，扶下殿。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day wuwu, the empress dowager assembled the hundred officials in the Qianyuan Hall; Pei Yan, with Vice Minister Liu Yizhi and Feathered Forest generals Cheng Wuting and Zhang Qianxu, led troops into the palace, proclaimed the empress dowager's order, deposed Zhongzong as Prince of Luling, and escorted him down from the hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuwu day, the empress dowager assembled officials in the Qianyuan Hall. Pei Yan, Liu Yizhi, and Feathered Forest generals Cheng Wuting and Zhang Qianxu led troops inside, proclaimed her order, deposed Zhongzong as Prince of Luling, and escorted him from the hall.

sentences.zh: 中宗曰：「我何罪？

translations.literal: Zhongzong said: "What is my crime?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong asked, "What crime have I committed?"

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「汝欲以天下與韋玄貞，何得無罪！

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "You wished to give the realm to Wei Xuanzhen—how can you be without crime!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager replied, "You meant to give the empire to Wei Xuanzhen—how are you not guilty?"

sentences.zh: 乃幽於別所。

translations.literal: He was then confined in a separate place.
translations.idiomatic: He was confined in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 己未，立雍州牧豫王旦為皇帝。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei the Prince of Yu, Dan, military commissioner of Yong Prefecture, was established as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day Prince Dan of Yu, commissioner of Yong Prefecture, was enthroned as emperor.

sentences.zh: 政事決於太后，居睿宗於別殿，不得有所預。

translations.literal: Government affairs were decided by the empress dowager; Ruizong was lodged in a separate hall and could take no part.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager held all power; Ruizong was lodged apart and allowed no part in rule.

sentences.zh: 立豫王妃劉氏為皇后。

translations.literal: The consort of the Prince of Yu, the Lady Liu, was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu, consort of the Prince of Yu, was made empress.

sentences.zh: 後，德威之孫也。

translations.literal: The empress was a granddaughter of Dewei.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was a granddaughter of Liu Dewei.

sentences.zh: 有飛騎十餘人飲於坊曲，一人言：「向知別無勳賞，不若奉廬陵。

translations.literal: More than ten courier riders were drinking in a ward lane; one said: "We now know there will be no rewards elsewhere—better to support Luling."
translations.idiomatic: A dozen courier riders were drinking in a lane when one said, "We know there'll be no rewards from this lot—better to back Luling."

sentences.zh: 」一人起，出詣北門告之。

translations.literal: One man rose, went out, and reported it at the north gate.
translations.idiomatic: One man rose and went to report it at the north gate.

sentences.zh: 座未散，皆捕得，系羽林獄，言者斬，餘以知反不告皆絞，告者除五品官。

translations.literal: Before the party had dispersed all were seized and imprisoned in the Feathered Forest jail; the speaker was beheaded, the rest for knowing of rebellion and not reporting were all strangled, and the informer was granted a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: Before the party broke up all were seized and jailed in the Feathered Forest prison. The speaker was beheaded; the rest, for knowing of treason and not reporting it, were strangled; the informer was given a fifth-rank post.

sentences.zh: 告密之端自此興矣。

translations.literal: The beginning of the system of informing was thus raised.
translations.idiomatic: Thus began the era of informers.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以永平郡王成器為皇太子，睿宗之長子。

translations.literal: On the day renzi Chengqian, Prince of Yongping, eldest son of Ruizong, was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day Chengqian, Prince of Yongping and Ruizong's eldest son, was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 赦天下，改元文明。

translations.literal: Amnesty was granted throughout the realm and the era name changed to Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era renamed Wenming.

sentences.zh: 庚申，廢皇太孫重照為庶人，命劉仁軌專知西京留守事。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen the imperial grand-son Chongzhao was deposed as a commoner; Liu Ren'gui was ordered exclusively to oversee the western capital's defense.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day the imperial grand-son Chongzhao was reduced to commoner status, and Liu Ren'gui was put in sole charge of the western capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 流韋玄貞於欽州。

translations.literal: Wei Xuanzhen was exiled to Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xuanzhen was exiled to Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太后與劉仁軌書曰：「昔漢以關中之事委蕭何，今托公亦猶是矣。

translations.literal: The empress dowager wrote to Liu Ren'gui: "Formerly Han entrusted the affairs of Guanzhong to Xiao He; today I entrust them to you in the same way."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager wrote to Liu Ren'gui: "Han once entrusted Guanzhong to Xiao He; I now entrust it to you in the same spirit."

sentences.zh: 」仁軌上疏，辭以衰老不堪居守，因陳呂後禍敗之事以申規戒。

translations.literal: Ren'gui submitted a memorial declining on grounds of age and infirmity unfit for garrison duty, and set forth the calamitous end of Empress Lü as admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Ren'gui memorialized that he was too old and frail for the post, and cited the ruin of Empress Lü as a warning.

sentences.zh: 太后使秘書監武承嗣繼璽書慰諭之曰：「今以皇帝諒闇不言，眇身且代親政；

translations.literal: The empress dowager had Secretariat Director Wu Chengsi follow with an imperial letter of comfort and instruction, saying: "Now because the emperor is in mourning and does not speak, I myself for the time being govern in his stead."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager had Secretariat Director Wu Chengsi reply with an imperial letter: "The emperor is in mourning and does not speak; I govern in his place for now."

sentences.zh: 遠勞勸戒，復辭衰疾。

translations.literal: You have taken great trouble with your admonition, yet again plead age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: You have gone to great pains to admonish me, yet again plead age and illness.

sentences.zh: 又云『呂氏見嗤於後代，祿、產貽禍於漢朝』，引喻良深，愧慰交集。

translations.literal: You also said, 'The Lü clan was mocked by later ages; Lu and Chan brought disaster on the Han house'—the analogy is very deep; shame and comfort are mingled.
translations.idiomatic: You also wrote that 'the Lü clan was mocked by posterity and Lu and Chan brought disaster on the Han'—a profound analogy that leaves me both shamed and comforted.

sentences.zh: 公忠貞之操，終始不渝，勁直之風，古今罕比。

translations.literal: Your loyal and upright conduct has never wavered from first to last; your forceful directness is rarely matched in past or present.
translations.idiomatic: Your loyalty has never wavered, and your blunt integrity is rarely matched in any age.

sentences.zh: 初聞此語，能不惘然；

translations.literal: At first hearing these words, how could one not be unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: At first your words unsettled me.

sentences.zh: 靜而思之，是為龜鏡。

translations.literal: Reflecting quietly on them, they are a tortoise mirror.
translations.idiomatic: On quiet reflection they are a mirror for the ages.

sentences.zh: 況公先朝舊德，遐邇具瞻，願以匡救為懷，無以暮年致請。

translations.literal: Moreover you are an old merit of the former court, looked to far and near; I wish you to keep rescue and correction at heart and not on account of old age make request to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: You are a pillar of the former court, admired throughout the realm. Keep the state's welfare at heart and do not plead old age to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，太后命左金吾將軍丘神勣詣巴州，檢校故太子賢宅，以備外虞，其實風使殺之。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou the empress dowager ordered Qiu Shenji, general of the Left Golden Guard, to go to Ba Prefecture to inspect the former residence of the deposed crown prince Xian, ostensibly to guard against external trouble, but in fact secretly instructed him to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day the empress dowager sent Qiu Shenji of the Left Golden Guard to Ba Prefecture to inspect the former crown prince Xian's residence, ostensibly for security but in fact to have him murdered.

sentences.zh: 神勣，行恭之子也。

translations.literal: Shenji was a son of Xinggong.
translations.idiomatic: Shenji was a son of Xinggong.

sentences.zh: 甲子，太后御武成殿，皇帝帥王公以下上尊號。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi the empress dowager presided in the Wucheng Hall; the emperor led the princes and dukes and those below in presenting a honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day the empress dowager presided in the Wucheng Hall while the emperor led the princes and officials in presenting her an honorific title.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，太后臨軒，遣禮部尚書武承嗣冊嗣皇帝。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao the empress dowager faced the throne hall and sent Minister of Rites Wu Chengsi to invest the heir emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day she faced the throne hall and sent Minister of Rites Wu Chengsi to invest the heir emperor.

sentences.zh: 自是太后常御紫宸殿，施慘紫帳以視朝。

translations.literal: From this time the empress dowager regularly presided in the Zichen Hall, setting a dark purple curtain to hold court.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter she regularly held court in the Zichen Hall behind a dark purple curtain.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以太常卿、檢校豫王府長史王德真為侍中；

translations.literal: On the day dingchou Wang Dezhen, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and acting chief administrator of the Prince of Yu's household, was made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day Wang Dezhen, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and acting chief administrator of the Prince of Yu's household, was made attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、檢校豫王府司馬劉禕之同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Liu Yizhi, Vice Minister of the Secretariat and acting military aide of the Prince of Yu's household, was made Associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yizhi, vice minister of the Secretariat and acting military aide of the Prince of Yu's household, was made third-rank associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁亥，徙杞王上金為畢王，鄱陽王素節為葛王。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day dinghai, Prince of Qi Shangjin was shifted to be Prince of Bi, and Prince of Poyang Sujie was shifted to be Prince of Ge.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dinghai day, Prince of Qi Shangjin was reassigned as Prince of Bi, and Prince of Poyang Sujie as Prince of Ge.

sentences.zh: 丘神勣至巴州，幽故太子賢於別室，逼令自殺。

translations.literal: Qiu Shenji arrived at Ba Prefecture, confined the former crown prince Xian in a separate chamber, and forced him to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiu Shenji reached Ba Prefecture, he shut the former crown prince Xian in a side room and drove him to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 太后乃歸罪於神勣，戊戌，舉哀於顯福門，貶神勣為疊州刺史。

translations.literal: The empress dowager then laid the blame on Shenji. On the day wuxu she held mourning at the Xianfu Gate and demoted Shenji to prefect of Die Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager then blamed Shenji. On wuxu day she staged mourning at the Xianfu Gate and demoted him to prefect of Die Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 己亥，追封賢為雍王。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, Xian was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day, Xian was posthumously created Prince of Yong.

sentences.zh: 神勣尋復入為左金吾將軍。

translations.literal: Before long Shenji was again summoned back to serve as general of the Left Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shenji was recalled to the capital as general of the Left Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，開府儀同三司、梁州都督滕王元嬰薨。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, Yuan Ying, Prince of Teng, Grand Preceptor with the honorary rank of Kaifu Yitong Sanqi and military governor of Liang Prefecture, died.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, in the fourth month, Yuan Ying, Prince of Teng—grand preceptor with the honorary rank of Kaifu Yitong Sanqi and military governor of Liang Prefecture—died.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，徙畢王上金為澤王，拜蘇州刺史；

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, Prince of Bi Shangjin was shifted to be Prince of Ze and appointed prefect of Su Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day, Prince of Bi Shangjin was reassigned as Prince of Ze and appointed prefect of Su Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 葛王素節為許王，拜絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Prince of Ge Sujie became Prince of Xu and was appointed prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ge Sujie was made Prince of Xu and appointed prefect of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，遷廬陵王於房州；

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, the Prince of Luling was moved to Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day, the Prince of Luling was transferred to Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，又遷於均州故濮王宅。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, he was moved again to the former residence of the Prince of Pu at Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day he was moved again, to the former residence of the Prince of Pu at Jun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙申，高宗靈駕西還。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day bingshen, Emperor Gaozong's funeral procession returned west.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingshen day, Emperor Gaozong's funeral cortege returned westward.

sentences.zh: 閏月，以禮部尚書武承嗣為太常卿、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Minister of Rites Wu Chengsi was made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Minister of Rites Wu Chengsi was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and third-rank associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊午，廣州都督路元睿為崑崙所殺。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day wuwu, Lu Yuanrui, military governor of Guangzhou Prefecture, was killed by Kunlun men.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, in the seventh month, on wuwu day, Lu Yuanrui, military governor of Guangzhou, was killed by Kunlun men.

sentences.zh: 元睿暗懦，僚屬恣橫，有商舶至，僚屬侵漁不已。

translations.literal: Yuanrui was dull and timid; his subordinates acted with reckless impunity. When merchant ships arrived, the subordinates endlessly extorted and preyed upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanrui was weak and indecisive, and his staff ran wild. Whenever merchant vessels put in, they preyed on them without end.

sentences.zh: 商胡訴於元睿，元睿索枷，欲系治之。

translations.literal: The merchant-traders complained to Yuanrui; Yuanrui demanded cangues and wished to bind and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The merchant-traders appealed to Yuanrui, who ordered cangues brought so he could bind and punish them.

sentences.zh: 群胡怒，有崑崙袖劍直登聽事，殺元睿及左右十餘人而去，無敢近者，登舟入海，追之不及。

translations.literal: The traders were enraged. One Kunlun man, sword hidden in his sleeve, strode straight into the office hall, killed Yuanrui and more than ten of those around him, and departed; none dared approach. He boarded a boat and put out to sea; pursuers could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: The traders flew into a rage. One Kunlun man, sword concealed in his sleeve, marched straight into the office hall, killed Yuanrui and more than ten of his attendants, and left—no one dared go near him. He boarded a ship and put out to sea, and pursuers could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 溫州大水，流四千餘家。

translations.literal: Great floods at Wen Prefecture swept away more than four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Severe flooding at Wen Prefecture carried off more than four thousand households.

sentences.zh: 突厥阿史那骨篤祿等寇朔州。

translations.literal: The Turks Ashina Gutulu and others raided Shuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks Ashina Gutulu and others attacked Shuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚寅，葬天皇大帝於乾隆，廟號高宗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day gengyin, the Celestial August Emperor was buried at Qianling; his temple title was Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengyin day, the Celestial August Emperor was buried at Qianling, with the temple title Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 初，尚書左丞馮元常為高宗所委，高宗晚年多疾，百司奏事，每曰：「朕體中不佳，可與元常平章以聞。

translations.literal: Earlier, Feng Yuanchang, Left Assistant Director in the Secretariat, had been entrusted by Emperor Gaozong. In Gaozong's later years he suffered many illnesses; when the hundred offices reported affairs, he would always say: "My body is not well; take counsel with Yuanchang and report back."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Feng Yuanchang, left assistant director in the Secretariat, had been a man Emperor Gaozong relied on. In his later years Gaozong was often ill; when the ministries reported business, he would say, "I am not well; discuss matters with Yuanchang and report back to me."

sentences.zh: 」元常嘗密言：「中宮威權太重，宜稍抑損。

translations.literal: Yuanchang once said privately: "The authority of the Central Palace is too heavy; it ought to be slightly reduced."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchang once said in private, "The empress's power is too great; it should be trimmed back somewhat."

sentences.zh: 」高宗雖不能用，深以其言為然。

translations.literal: Although Emperor Gaozong could not act on his words, he deeply agreed with the point.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong could not follow his advice, but he deeply agreed with it.

sentences.zh: 及太后稱制，四方爭言符瑞；

translations.literal: When the empress dowager assumed the regency, throughout the realm people vied to report auspicious omens.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empress dowager assumed the regency, people everywhere competed to report auspicious omens.

sentences.zh: 嵩陽令樊文獻瑞石，太后命於朝堂示百官，元常奏：「狀涉諂詐，不可誣罔天下。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Songyang, Fan Wen, presented an auspicious stone. The empress dowager ordered it displayed in the court hall to all the officials. Yuanchang memorialized: "The inscription smacks of flattery and fraud; one must not deceive the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wen, magistrate of Songyang, presented an auspicious stone. The empress dowager ordered it shown in the court hall to the officials. Yuanchang memorialized, "The inscription reeks of flattery and deceit; the realm must not be misled."

sentences.zh: 」太后不悅，出為隴州刺史。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was displeased and had him sent out to serve as prefect of Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was displeased and sent him out to serve as prefect of Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元常，子琮之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yuanchang was a great-grandson of Feng Zicong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchang was a great-grandson of Feng Zicong.

sentences.zh: 丙午，太常卿、同中書門下三品武承嗣罷為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, Wu Chengsi, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the third rank, was removed from his posts and made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day, Wu Chengsi was removed as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and third-rank associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery and made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 括州大水，流二千餘家。

translations.literal: Great floods at Kuo Prefecture swept away more than two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Severe flooding at Kuo Prefecture carried off more than two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲寅，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day jiayin, amnesty was granted throughout the realm and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiayin day, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign era was changed.

sentences.zh: 旗幟皆從金色。

translations.literal: Banners and flags all turned to gold.
translations.idiomatic: Banners and flags were all changed to gold.

sentences.zh: 八品以下，舊服青者更服碧。

translations.literal: Those of the eighth rank and below who formerly wore blue were to wear green instead.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the eighth rank and below who had worn blue were now to wear green.

sentences.zh: 改東都為神都，宮名太初。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital was renamed the Divine Capital; the palace was named Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital was renamed the Divine Capital, and the palace was called Taichu.

sentences.zh: 又改尚書省為文昌台，左、右僕射為左、右相，六曹為天、地、四時六官；

translations.literal: The Secretariat was also renamed the Wenchang Bureau; the left and right vice directors became the left and right chancellors; the six bureaus became the six officials of Heaven, Earth, and the Four Seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was renamed the Wenchang Bureau; the left and right vice directors became the left and right chancellors; and the six bureaus became the six officials of Heaven, Earth, and the Four Seasons.

sentences.zh: 門下省為鸞台，中書省為鳳閣，侍中為納言，中書令為內史；

translations.literal: The Chancellery became the Luantai; the Secretariat became the Fengge; attendant-in-ordinary became nayan; Secretariat Director became neishi.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellery became the Luantai, the Secretariat the Fengge, attendant-in-ordinary became nayan, and the Secretariat director became neishi.

sentences.zh: 御史台為左肅政台，增置右肅政台；

translations.literal: The Censorate became the Left Zhengyi Bureau; a Right Zhengyi Bureau was additionally established.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate became the Left Zhengyi Bureau, and a Right Zhengyi Bureau was added.

sentences.zh: 其餘省、寺、監、率之名，悉以義類改之。

translations.literal: All other names of ministries, courts, directorates, and directorates of palace services were entirely changed according to categories of meaning.
