translations.idiomatic: The names of all other ministries, courts, directorates, and palace offices were likewise changed according to their symbolic meaning.

sentences.zh: 以左武衛大將軍程務挺為單于道安撫大使，以備突厥。

translations.literal: Grand General of the Left Martial Guard Cheng Wuting was made Pacification Commissioner of the Chanyu Circuit to guard against the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wuting, grand general of the Left Martial Guard, was appointed pacification commissioner of the Chanyu Circuit to guard against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 武承嗣請太后追王其祖，立武氏七廟，太后從之。

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi asked the empress dowager to posthumously ennoble her ancestors as kings and establish a seven-temple ancestral shrine for the Wu clan; the empress dowager agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi asked the empress dowager to posthumously create her ancestors as kings and establish a seven-temple shrine for the Wu clan, and she agreed.

sentences.zh: 裴炎諫曰：「太后母臨天下，當示至公，不可私於所親。

translations.literal: Pei Yan remonstrated: "The empress dowager as mother of the realm ought to show utmost impartiality and must not favor her own kin."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yan remonstrated, "As mother of the realm, Your Majesty should show the utmost impartiality and must not show partiality to your own kin."

sentences.zh: 獨不見呂氏之敗乎！

translations.literal: Have you not seen how the Lü clan came to ruin!
translations.idiomatic: Have you not seen how the Lü clan met its ruin!

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「呂後以權委生者，故及於敗。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "Empress Lü entrusted power to the living; that is why she met ruin."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Empress Lü entrusted power to the living—that is why she fell."

sentences.zh: 今吾追尊亡者，何傷乎！

translations.literal: Now I am posthumously honoring the dead—what harm is there!
translations.idiomatic: Now I am honoring the dead—what harm can that do!

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「事當防微杜漸，不可長耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "Matters should be halted at the first sign; one must not let them grow."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Evils should be stopped at the first sign; they must not be allowed to grow."

sentences.zh: 」太后不從。

translations.literal: The empress dowager did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager would not listen.

sentences.zh: 己巳，追尊太后五代祖克己為魯靖公，妣為夫人；

translations.literal: On the day jisi, the empress dowager's fifth-generation ancestor Keji was posthumously ennobled as Lord Jing of Lu, and his wife as Lady.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day, the empress dowager's fifth-generation ancestor Keji was posthumously created Lord Jing of Lu, and his wife Lady.

sentences.zh: 高祖居常為太尉、北平恭肅王，曾祖儉為太尉、金城義康王，祖華為太尉、太原安成王，考士擭為太師、魏定王；

translations.literal: Great-great-grandfather Juchang was made Grand Commandant and Prince Gongsu of Beiping; great-grandfather Jian was made Grand Commandant and Prince Yikang of Jincheng; grandfather Hua was made Grand Commandant and Prince Ancheng of Taiyuan; father Shiyi was made Grand Preceptor and Prince Ding of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-great-grandfather Juchang was made grand commandant and Prince Gongsu of Beiping; her great-grandfather Jian, grand commandant and Prince Yikang of Jincheng; her grandfather Hua, grand commandant and Prince Ancheng of Taiyuan; and her father Shiyi, grand preceptor and Prince Ding of Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖妣皆為妃。

translations.literal: All the ancestral wives were made consorts.
translations.idiomatic: All the ancestral wives were created consorts.

sentences.zh: 裴炎由是得罪。

translations.literal: Pei Yan thereby fell into disfavor.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yan thereby fell from favor.

sentences.zh: 又作五代祠堂於文水。

translations.literal: A shrine to five generations was also built at Wenshui.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine to five generations was also built at Wenshui.

sentences.zh: 時諸武用事，唐宗室人人自危，眾心憤惋。

translations.literal: At this time the Wu clan held power; every member of the Tang imperial house feared for himself, and popular resentment smoldered.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Wu clan held power; every member of the Tang imperial house lived in fear, and public anger ran high.

sentences.zh: 會眉州刺史英公李敬業及弟盩厔令敬猷、給事中唐之奇、長安主簿駱賓王、詹事司直杜求仁皆坐事，敬業貶柳州司馬，敬猷免官，之奇貶括蒼令，賓王貶臨海丞，求仁貶黟令。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Jingye, Duke of Ying and prefect of Mei Prefecture, together with his brother Jingyou, magistrate of Zhouzhi County, Tang Zhiqi, a drafter in the Secretariat, Luo Binwang, chief clerk of Chang'an, and Du Qiuren, a judicial officer in the Crown Prince's household, were all punished for offenses: Jingye was demoted to military aide at Liuzhou, Jingyou was stripped of office, Zhiqi was demoted to magistrate of Kuocang, Binwang to assistant magistrate of Linhai, and Qiuren to magistrate of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened, Li Jingye, Duke of Ying and prefect of Mei Prefecture, his brother Jingyou, magistrate of Zhouzhi County, Tang Zhiqi, a drafting attendant, Luo Binwang, chief clerk of Chang'an, and Du Qiuren, a judicial officer in the crown prince's household, had all been punished for various offenses: Jingye was demoted to military aide at Liuzhou, Jingyou dismissed, Zhiqi sent to Kuocang as magistrate, Binwang to Linhai as assistant magistrate, and Qiuren to Yi as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 求仁，正倫之侄也。

translations.literal: Qiuren was a nephew of Du Zhenglun.
translations.idiomatic: Qiuren was a nephew of Du Zhenglun.

sentences.zh: 盩厔尉魏思溫嘗為御史，復被黜。

translations.literal: Wei Siwen, the magistrate of Zhouzhi County, had once served as a censor and was again dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Siwen, magistrate of Zhouzhi County, had once served as a censor and had again been dismissed.

sentences.zh: 皆會於揚州，各自以失職怨望，乃謀作亂，以匡復廬陵王為辭。

translations.literal: They all gathered at Yang Prefecture, each nursing grievances over loss of office, and plotted rebellion, taking restoration of the Prince of Luling as their pretext.
translations.idiomatic: They all met at Yang Prefecture, each bitter over loss of office, and plotted rebellion under the banner of restoring the Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 思溫為之謀主，使其黨監察御史薛仲璋求奉使江都，令雍州人韋超詣仲璋告變，云「揚州長史陳敬之謀反」。

translations.literal: Siwen was their chief strategist. He had his follower, investigating censor Xue Zhongzhang, seek an imperial mission to Jiangdu, and had Wei Chao of Yong Prefecture go to Zhongzhang to report a plot, saying "Yang Prefecture chief administrator Chen Jingzhi is plotting rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Siwen was their chief strategist. He had his follower, investigating censor Xue Zhongzhang, obtain an imperial mission to Jiangdu, and sent Wei Chao of Yong Prefecture to Zhongzhang to report a conspiracy, claiming that "Yang Prefecture chief administrator Chen Jingzhi is plotting rebellion."

sentences.zh: 仲璋收敬之繫獄。

translations.literal: Zhongzhang arrested Jingzhi and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhang arrested Jingzhi and threw him in prison.

sentences.zh: 居數日，敬業乘傳而至，矯稱揚州司馬來之官，云「奉密旨，以高州酋長馮子猷謀反，發兵討之。

translations.literal: After several days Jingye arrived by post relay, falsely claiming to be the Yang Prefecture military aide coming to take office, and saying "By secret edict, because the chieftain of Gaozhou, Feng Ziyou, is plotting rebellion, troops are to be raised to suppress him."
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Jingye arrived by post relay, falsely claiming to be the Yang Prefecture military aide reporting for duty, and announcing, "By secret edict, because Feng Ziyou, chieftain of Gaozhou, is plotting rebellion, I am to raise troops to suppress him."

sentences.zh: 」於是開府庫，令士曹參軍李宗臣就錢坊，驅囚徒、工匠數百，授以甲。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened the prefectural storehouses and ordered the staff officer Li Zongchen to go to the mint, drive out several hundred convicts and artisans, and arm them.
translations.idiomatic: He then opened the prefectural storehouses and ordered staff officer Li Zongchen to the mint, where he rounded up several hundred convicts and artisans and issued them armor.

sentences.zh: 斬敬之於系所；

translations.literal: Jingzhi was beheaded in the place of imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhi was beheaded in prison.

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍孫處行拒之，亦斬以徇，僚吏無敢動者。

translations.literal: The recording officer Sun Xuchu resisted and was also beheaded as a warning; none of the staff dared move.
translations.idiomatic: Recording officer Sun Xuchu tried to resist and was beheaded as an example; none of the staff dared stir.

sentences.zh: 遂起一州之兵，復稱嗣聖元年。

translations.literal: Thereupon he raised the troops of the whole prefecture and again proclaimed the first year of the Sishèng era.
translations.idiomatic: He then raised the entire prefecture's forces and proclaimed the first year of the Sishèng era.

sentences.zh: 開三府，一曰匡復府，二曰英公府，三曰揚州大都督府。

translations.literal: Three offices were opened: the first called the Restoration Office, the second the Duke of Ying Office, and the third the Yangzhou Grand Military Governor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: He opened three headquarters: the Restoration Office, the Duke of Ying Office, and the Yangzhou Grand Military Governor's Office.

sentences.zh: 敬業自稱匡復府上將，領揚州大都督。

translations.literal: Jingye styled himself supreme general of the Restoration Office and took command as grand military governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye styled himself supreme general of the Restoration Office and assumed the post of grand military governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以之奇、求仁為左、右長史，宗臣、仲璋為左、右司馬，思溫為軍師，賓王為記室，旬日間得勝兵十餘萬。

translations.literal: Zhiqi and Qiuren were made left and right chief administrators; Zongchen and Zhongzhang were made left and right military aides; Siwen was made strategist; Binwang was made secretary; and within ten days more than one hundred thousand battle-ready troops were gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiqi and Qiuren became left and right chief administrators; Zongchen and Zhongzhang, left and right military aides; Siwen, strategist; and Binwang, secretary. Within ten days he had assembled more than one hundred thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 移檄州縣，略曰：「偽臨朝武氏者，人非溫順，地實寒微。

translations.literal: A proclamation was sent to the prefectures and counties, stating in part: "The false ruler holding court, the Wu woman, is by nature not gentle and compliant, and by origin truly low and humble."
translations.idiomatic: He sent a proclamation to the prefectures and counties, which read in part: "The usurper holding court, the Wu woman, is neither gentle by nature nor noble by birth."

sentences.zh: 昔充太宗下陳，嘗以更衣入侍，洎乎晚節，穢亂春宮。

translations.literal: In the past she served among Emperor Taizong's lower attendants and once entered his service to change his garments; in her later years she defiled the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Once she served among Emperor Taizong's attendants and entered his chambers to change his garments; in her later years she brought corruption into the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 密隱先帝之私，陰圖後庭之嬖，踐元後於翬翟，陷吾君於聚麀。

translations.literal: She secretly concealed the late emperor's private affairs and covertly plotted the favors of the inner quarters; she trod upon the primary consort in her phoenix robes and trapped our lord in incestuous disorder.
translations.idiomatic: She hid the late emperor's secrets, plotted for power in the inner quarters, trampled the empress in her phoenix robes, and trapped our sovereign in incestuous shame.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「殺姊屠兄，弒君鴆母，人神之所同嫉，天地之所不容。

translations.literal: It also said: "She killed her elder sister, slaughtered her elder brothers, murdered her sovereign and poisoned her mother—what gods and men alike detest, what heaven and earth cannot tolerate."
translations.idiomatic: It continued: "She killed her elder sister, butchered her elder brothers, murdered her sovereign and poisoned her mother—an outrage hated by gods and men alike, intolerable to heaven and earth."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「包藏禍心，竊窺神器。

translations.literal: It also said: "She harbors a treacherous heart and covets the imperial regalia in secret."
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "She harbors treacherous intent and secretly covets the throne."

sentences.zh: 君之愛子，幽之於別宮；

translations.literal: The ruler's beloved son she confines in a separate palace.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign's beloved son she keeps confined in a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 賊之宗盟，委之以重任。

translations.literal: The traitor's kinsmen she entrusts with weighty responsibilities.
translations.idiomatic: While the traitor's own kin she loads with heavy office.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「一抔之土未干，六尺之孤安在！

translations.literal: It also said: "The mound of earth is not yet dry, and where is the six-foot orphan!"
translations.idiomatic: It also cried: "The grave mound is not yet dry—where is the orphaned heir!"

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「試觀今日之域中，竟是誰家之天下！

translations.literal: It also said: "Look upon the realm today—whose empire is it in the end!"
translations.idiomatic: It also demanded: "Look upon the realm today—whose empire is it, in the end!"

sentences.zh: 」太后見檄，問曰：「誰所為？

translations.literal: When the empress dowager saw the proclamation, she asked: "Who wrote this?"
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager saw the proclamation, she asked, "Who wrote this?"

sentences.zh: 」或對曰：「駱賓王。

translations.literal: Someone answered: "Luo Binwang."
translations.idiomatic: Someone answered, "Luo Binwang."

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「宰相之過也。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "This is the fault of the chief ministers."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "This is the fault of the chief ministers."

sentences.zh: 人有如此才，而使之流落不偶乎！

translations.literal: A man with such talent, and yet he is left to drift without fitting employment!
translations.idiomatic: A man of such talent, and yet he was left to wander without proper appointment!

sentences.zh: 敬業求得人貌類故太子賢者，紿眾云：「賢不死，亡在此城中，令吾屬舉兵。

translations.literal: Jingye found a man whose appearance resembled the former crown prince Xian and deceived the crowd, saying: "Xian is not dead; he has fled and is in this city, and has ordered us to raise troops."
translations.idiomatic: Jingye found a man who looked like the former crown prince Xian and deceived the crowd, claiming, "Xian is not dead—he has fled here and ordered us to take up arms."

sentences.zh: 」因奉以號令。

translations.literal: He was then installed to issue commands.
translations.idiomatic: They then installed him to issue commands.

sentences.zh: 楚州司馬李崇福帥所部三縣應敬業。

translations.literal: Li Chongfu, military aide of Chuzhou, led the three counties under his command to join Jingye.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongfu, military aide of Chuzhou, led the three counties under his command to answer Jingye's call.

sentences.zh: 盱眙人劉行舉獨據縣不從，敬業遣其將尉遲昭攻盱眙，行舉拒卻之。

translations.literal: Liu Xingju of Xuyi alone held his county and refused to follow; Jingye sent his general Yuchi Zhao to attack Xuyi, and Xingju repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xingju of Xuyi alone held his county and refused to join; Jingye sent his general Yuchi Zhao against Xuyi, but Xingju drove him off.

sentences.zh: 詔以行舉為游擊將軍，以其弟行實為楚州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict made Xingju mobile corps general and appointed his younger brother Xingshi prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Xingju mobile corps general and appointed his younger brother Xingshi prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以左玉鈐衛大將軍李孝逸為揚州道大總管，將兵三十萬，以將軍李知士、馬敬臣為之副，以討李敬業。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, Li Xiaoyi, grand general of the Left Jade Talisman Guard, was made grand commander of the Yangzhou Circuit with three hundred thousand troops; Generals Li Zhishi and Ma Jingchen were made his deputies, to suppress Li Jingye.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day, Li Xiaoyi, grand general of the Left Jade Talisman Guard, was appointed grand commander of the Yangzhou Circuit at the head of three hundred thousand troops, with Generals Li Zhishi and Ma Jingchen as his deputies, to suppress Li Jingye.

sentences.zh: 武承嗣與從父弟右衛將軍三思以韓王元嘉、魯王靈夔屬尊位重，屢勸太后因事誅之。

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi and his paternal cousin, Right Guard General Sansi, because Princes of Han Yuangjia and Lu Lingqi were of honored rank and heavy standing, repeatedly urged the empress dowager to find occasion to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi and his cousin, Right Guard General Sansi, repeatedly urged the empress dowager to find occasion to execute Princes of Han Yuangjia and Lu Lingqi, whose rank and standing were exalted.

sentences.zh: 太后謀於執政，劉禕之、韋思謙皆無言；

translations.literal: The empress dowager consulted the chief ministers; Liu Yizhi and Wei Siqian both said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager consulted the chief ministers; Liu Yizhi and Wei Siqian both kept silent.

sentences.zh: 內史裴炎獨固爭，太后愈不悅。

translations.literal: Neishi Pei Yan alone firmly remonstrated; the empress dowager grew all the more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Neishi Pei Yan alone argued firmly against it, and the empress dowager grew still more displeased.

sentences.zh: 三思，元慶之子也。

translations.literal: Sansi was a son of Yuanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi was a son of Yuanqing.

sentences.zh: 及李敬業舉兵，薛仲璋，炎之甥也，炎欲示閒暇，不汲汲議誅討。

translations.literal: When Li Jingye raised troops, Xue Zhongzhang, who was Pei Yan's nephew, was among them; Yan wished to appear at ease and did not urgently discuss suppression and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jingye rose in arms, Xue Zhongzhang—Pei Yan's nephew—was among the rebels; Yan wished to appear unhurried and did not press for immediate discussion of suppression.

sentences.zh: 太后問計於炎，對曰：「皇帝年長，不親政事，故豎子得以為辭。

translations.literal: The empress dowager asked Yan for a plan; he replied: "The emperor is already grown and does not personally handle affairs of government; that is why this upstart has found a pretext."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager asked Yan for counsel. He replied, "The emperor is already grown and does not personally govern; that is why this upstart has found a pretext."

sentences.zh: 若太后返政，則不討自平矣。

translations.literal: If the empress dowager returns the regency, then without suppressing them the rebellion will settle of itself.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty returns power, the rebellion will collapse without need of suppression.

sentences.zh: 」監察御史藍田崔察聞之，上言：「炎受顧托，大權在己，若無異圖，何故請太后歸政？

translations.literal: Investigating censor Cui Cha of Lantian, hearing this, memorialized: "Yan received the late emperor's entrustment; great power is in his own hands. If he has no ulterior design, why does he ask the empress dowager to return the regency?"
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Cui Cha of Lantian, hearing this, memorialized, "Yan received the late emperor's dying charge and holds great power in his own hands. If he harbors no ulterior design, why does he ask the empress dowager to return power?"

sentences.zh: 」太后命左肅政大夫金城騫味道、侍御史櫟陽魚承曄鞫之，收炎下獄。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered Left Zhengyi Grand Counselor Qian Weidao of Jincheng and attendant censor Yu Chengye of Liyang to interrogate him, and Yan was arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered Left Zhengyi Grand Counselor Qian Weidao of Jincheng and attendant censor Yu Chengye of Liyang to investigate, and Yan was arrested and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 炎被收，辭氣不屈。

translations.literal: When Yan was arrested, his words and bearing did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was arrested, he did not yield in word or bearing.

sentences.zh: 或勸炎遜辭以免，炎曰：「宰相下獄，安有全理！

translations.literal: Someone urged Yan to use humble words to escape punishment; Yan said: "When a chief minister enters prison, how can there be any prospect of coming out whole!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Yan to humble himself to save his life. Yan said, "When a chief minister is thrown into prison, how can he expect to survive intact!"

sentences.zh: 鳳閣舍人李景諶證炎必反。

translations.literal: Fengge Secretariat Officer Li Jingchen testified that Yan would certainly rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Fengge secretariat officer Li Jingchen testified that Yan was certainly plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 劉景先及鳳閣侍郎義陽胡元范皆曰：「炎，社稷元臣，有功於國，悉心奉上，天下所知，臣敢明其不反。

translations.literal: Liu Jingxian and Fengge Vice Minister Hu Yuanfan of Yiyang both said: "Yan is a pillar minister of the state, who has served the realm with merit, devoted himself in service to the throne, and is known throughout the realm; your subject dares affirm that he is not rebelling."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jingxian and Fengge vice minister Hu Yuanfan of Yiyang both said, "Yan is a pillar minister of the state who has served the realm with distinction and devoted himself to the throne—this is known to all. I dare affirm that he is not rebelling."

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「炎反有端，顧卿不知耳。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "Yan's rebellion has its grounds; you simply do not know them."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Yan's rebellion has its grounds—you simply do not know them."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「若裴炎為反，則臣等亦反也。

translations.literal: They replied: "If Pei Yan is rebelling, then we too are rebelling."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "If Pei Yan is a rebel, then so are we."

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「朕知裴炎反，知卿等不反。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "I know Pei Yan is rebelling; I know you are not rebelling."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "I know Pei Yan is plotting rebellion—I know you are not."

sentences.zh: 」文武間證炎不反者甚眾，太后皆不聽。

translations.literal: Many among the civil and military officials testified between themselves that Yan was not rebelling; the empress dowager would hear none of it.
translations.idiomatic: Many civil and military officials came forward to attest that Yan was no rebel, but the Empress Dowager would hear none of it.

sentences.zh: 俄並景先、元范下獄。

translations.literal: Before long both Jingxian and Yuanfan were thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Before long both Liu Jingxian and Hu Yuanfan were thrown into prison as well.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以騫味道檢校內史同鳳閣鸞台三品，李景諶同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: On dinghai day, Qian Weidao was made acting interior secretary with third rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Tower, and Li Jingchen was made associate director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Tower.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day, Qian Weidao was appointed acting Interior Secretary at third rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Tower, and Li Jingchen was made Associate Director of the same offices.

sentences.zh: 魏思溫說李敬業曰：「明公以匡復為辭，宜帥大眾鼓行而進，直指洛陽，則天下知公志在勤王，四面響應矣。

translations.literal: Wei Siwen urged Li Jingye, saying: "Your lordship takes restoration as your banner; you ought to lead the mass of troops beating drums as you advance, striking straight for Luoyang—then all under Heaven will know your aim is to rescue the throne, and responses will come from every quarter."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Siwen urged Li Jingye: "Your lordship marches under the banner of restoration. Lead your main force forward with drums beating, straight for Luoyang—the realm will see that your heart is with the throne, and support will rise on every side."

sentences.zh: 」薛仲璋曰：「金陵有王氣，且大江天險，足以為固，不如先取常、潤，為定霸之基，然後北向以圖中原，進無不利，退有所歸，此良策也！

translations.literal: Xue Zhongzhang said: "Jinling bears the aura of kingship, and the Great River's natural barrier is enough to make it secure. Better first to seize Chang and Run as a foundation for establishing hegemony, then turn north to contend for the Central Plains—advancing you will meet no obstacle, retreating you will have a place to return. This is the superior strategy!"
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhongzhang said, "Jinling has the aura of empire, and the Yangtze is a heaven-sent rampart strong enough to hold. Seize Changzhou and Runzhou first and lay the foundations of rule; then turn north toward the heartland. Advance, and nothing will stand in your way; retreat, and you will still have a refuge. That is the wise course!"

sentences.zh: 」思溫曰：「山東豪傑以武氏專制，憤惋不平，聞公舉事，皆自蒸麥飯為糧，伸鋤為兵，以俟南軍之至。

translations.literal: Siwen said: "The bold spirits east of the mountains, chafing at the Wu clan's monopoly of power, upon hearing of your raising forces all steam wheat for rations and take up hoes as weapons, waiting for the southern army to arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Siwen replied, "The champions of Shandong seethe under the Wu clan's grip. When they hear that you have risen, they steam their own wheat for rations and turn hoes into spears, waiting only for your army to cross the Huai."

sentences.zh: 不乘此勢以立大功，乃更蓄縮，欲自謀巢穴，遠近聞之，其誰不解體！

translations.literal: If you fail to ride this momentum to win great achievements but instead hold back, seeking only to carve out a nest for yourselves—when near and far hear of it, who will not lose heart!
translations.idiomatic: If you fail to seize this tide and win a great victory, but hang back instead to dig yourselves a private nest, who near or far will not lose heart when they hear of it?

sentences.zh: 」敬業不從，使唐之奇守江都，將兵渡江攻潤州。

translations.literal: Jingye did not follow this advice. He sent Tang Zhiqi to hold Jiangdu and led troops across the river to attack Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye would not listen. He left Tang Zhiqi to hold Jiangdu and led his army across the river to attack Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 思溫謂杜求仁曰：「兵勢合則強，分則弱，敬業不並力渡淮，收山東之眾以取洛陽，敗在眼中矣！

translations.literal: Siwen said to Du Qiuren: "When military momentum is united it is strong; divided, weak. Jingye does not concentrate his strength to cross the Huai, gather the masses east of the mountains, and take Luoyang—defeat is before our very eyes!"
translations.idiomatic: Siwen told Du Qiuren, "United, an army is strong; divided, it is weak. Jingye will not mass his strength to cross the Huai, rally Shandong, and take Luoyang—defeat is already in sight!"

sentences.zh: 壬辰，敬業陷潤州，執刺史李思文，以李宗臣代之。

translations.literal: On renchen day, Jingye captured Run Prefecture, seized the prefect Li Siwen, and replaced him with Li Zongchen.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day, Jingye took Runzhou, seized its prefect Li Siwen, and installed Li Zongchen in his place.

sentences.zh: 思文，敬業之叔父也，知敬業之謀，先遣使間道上變，為敬業所攻，拒守久之，力屈而陷。

translations.literal: Siwen was Jingye's uncle. Learning of Jingye's plot, he had first sent a messenger by a secret route to report the rebellion. Jingye attacked him; he held out for a long time, but strength failed and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Siwen was Jingye's uncle. Forewarned of the plot, he had already sent a messenger by a hidden route to report the uprising. Jingye besieged him; he held out for a long time, but at last his strength gave out and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 思溫請斬以徇，敬業不許，謂思文曰：「叔黨於武氏，宜改姓武。

translations.literal: Siwen asked to have him beheaded as a warning, but Jingye would not permit it. He said to Siwen: "Uncle, you sided with the Wu clan—you ought to change your surname to Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Siwen urged that he be executed to set an example, but Jingye refused and told Siwen, "Uncle, you sided with the Wu clan—you ought to take the surname Wu."

sentences.zh: 」潤州司馬劉延嗣不降，敬業將斬之，思溫救之，得免，與思文皆囚於獄中。

translations.literal: Run Prefecture aide Liu Yansi would not submit. Jingye was about to execute him, but Siwen saved him and he was spared. Both he and Siwen were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yansi, Runzhou's military aide, refused to surrender. Jingye was about to execute him, but Wei Siwen intervened and he was spared. Both men were thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 劉延嗣，審禮從父弟也。

translations.literal: Liu Yansi was a cousin of Shenli on his father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yansi was a paternal cousin of Liu Shenli.

sentences.zh: 曲阿令河間尹元貞引兵救潤州，戰敗，為敬業所擒，臨以白刃，不屈而死。

translations.literal: Qu'e magistrate Yin Yuanzhen of Hejian led troops to relieve Run Prefecture. Defeated in battle, he was captured by Jingye. With naked blades at his throat he would not yield and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yuanzhen of Hejian, magistrate of Qu'e, marched to relieve Runzhou but was defeated and captured by Jingye. With blades at his throat he would not bow—and died where he stood.

sentences.zh: 丙申，斬裴炎於都亭。

translations.literal: On bingshen day, Pei Yan was executed at Duting.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day, Pei Yan was beheaded at Duting.

sentences.zh: 炎將死，顧兄弟曰：「兄弟官皆自致，炎無分毫之力，今坐炎流竄，不亦悲乎！

translations.literal: As Yan was about to die, he turned to his brothers and said: "You brothers all won your offices on your own merits; Yan contributed not the slightest effort. Yet now because of Yan you are to be banished—is this not lamentable!"
translations.idiomatic: Facing death, Yan turned to his brothers and said, "You earned your offices by your own merit—I had no hand in it. Yet now you are to be banished on my account. Is that not a bitter thing?"

sentences.zh: 」籍沒其家，無甔石之儲。

translations.literal: His household goods were confiscated, yet he had not even a single jar's store of grain.
translations.idiomatic: His property was confiscated, yet his house held scarcely a jar of grain.

sentences.zh: 劉景先貶普州刺史，又貶辰州刺史，胡元范流瓊州而死。

translations.literal: Liu Jingxian was demoted to prefect of Puzhou, then demoted again to prefect of Chenzhou. Hu Yuanfan was exiled to Qiongzhou and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jingxian was demoted to prefect of Puzhou, then demoted again to prefect of Chenzhou. Hu Yuanfan was exiled to Qiongzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 裴炎弟子太僕寺丞胄先，年十七，上封事請見言事。

translations.literal: Pei Yan's nephew Zhouxian, a deputy in the Grand Stable Office, aged seventeen, submitted a sealed memorial requesting an audience to speak on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhouxian, Yan's seventeen-year-old nephew and a deputy in the Grand Stable Office, submitted a sealed memorial asking for an audience to address affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 太后召見，詰之曰：「汝伯父謀反，尚何言？

translations.literal: The empress dowager summoned him and interrogated him, saying: "Your uncle plotted rebellion—what more have you to say?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager summoned him and demanded, "Your uncle plotted rebellion—what more do you have to say?"

sentences.zh: 」胄先曰：「臣為陛下畫計耳，安敢訴冤！

translations.literal: Zhouxian said: "Your subject merely wishes to lay out a plan for Your Majesty—how would he dare appeal his grievance!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxian answered, "I come only to offer counsel to Your Majesty—how would I dare plead my family's case!"

sentences.zh: 陛下為李氏婦，先帝棄天下，遽攬朝政，變易嗣子，疏斥李氏，封崇諸武。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is a daughter-in-law of the Li clan. When the late emperor departed this world, you suddenly seized hold of court governance, changed the heir, pushed aside the Li clan, and ennobled the various Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is a daughter-in-law of the Li house. When the late emperor died, you seized the reins of government, changed the heir, cast aside the Li clan, and raised up the Wu.

sentences.zh: 臣伯父忠於社稷，反誣以罪，戮及子孫。

translations.literal: My uncle was loyal to the state, yet he was falsely charged with crime, and slaughter extended to his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: My uncle served the realm in good faith, yet he was condemned on false charges, and punishment reached even his descendants.

sentences.zh: 陛下所為如是，臣實惜之！

translations.literal: What Your Majesty has done is such that your subject truly deplores it!
translations.idiomatic: What Your Majesty has done fills me with sorrow!

sentences.zh: 陛下早宜復子明辟，高枕深居，則宗族可全；

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought early to restore the son and make clear the return of power, then rest at ease in deep seclusion—then the clan may be preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should restore the son and return power to him, then rest secure in seclusion—the clan may yet be preserved whole.

sentences.zh: 不然，天下一變，不可復救矣！

translations.literal: Otherwise, once the realm shifts, it cannot be saved!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, when the realm turns against you, nothing will save it!

sentences.zh: 」太后怒曰：「胡白，小子敢發此言！

translations.literal: The empress dowager angrily said: "Nonsense—how dare a stripling utter words like these!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager flared with anger. "Nonsense! How dare a stripling speak such words!"

sentences.zh: 」命引出。

translations.literal: She ordered him led out.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered him taken out.

sentences.zh: 胄先反顧曰：「今用臣言，猶未晚！

translations.literal: Zhouxian looked back and said: "If you heed my words now, it is still not too late!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxian looked back and cried, "If you heed my counsel now, it is still not too late!"

sentences.zh: 」如是者三。

translations.literal: He said this three times.
translations.idiomatic: He said this three times over.

sentences.zh: 太后命於朝堂杖之一百，長流瀼州。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered him beaten one hundred strokes in the court hall and exiled far to Rang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager ordered him flogged one hundred strokes in the audience hall and exiled to distant Rangzhou.

sentences.zh: 炎之下獄也，郎將姜嗣宗使至長安，劉仁軌問以東都事，嗣宗曰：「嗣宗覺裴炎有異於常久矣。

translations.literal: When Yan was thrown into prison, a commandant's officer Jiang Zizong arrived as envoy in Chang'an. Liu Ren'gui asked him about affairs in the Eastern Capital. Zizong said: "Zizong perceived Pei Yan as abnormal for a long time now."
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was imprisoned, commandant Jiang Zizong arrived in Chang'an on embassy. Liu Ren'gui questioned him about affairs in the Eastern Capital. Zizong said, "I had long noticed that Pei Yan was not himself."

sentences.zh: 」仁軌曰：「使人覺之邪？

translations.literal: Ren'gui said: "Was it your mission that made you perceive it?"
translations.idiomatic: Ren'gui asked, "Was it your mission that made you notice?"

sentences.zh: 」嗣宗曰：「然。

translations.literal: Zizong said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: Zizong said, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 」仁軌曰：「仁軌有奏事，願附使人以聞。

translations.literal: Ren'gui said: "Ren'gui has a matter to memorialize and wishes to send it by your envoy to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Ren'gui said, "I have a memorial to submit. May I send it back with your embassy?"

sentences.zh: 」嗣宗曰：「諾。

translations.literal: Zizong said: "Agreed."
translations.idiomatic: Zizong agreed.

sentences.zh: 」明日，受仁軌表而還，表言：「嗣宗知裴炎反不言。

translations.literal: The next day he received Ren'gui's memorial and returned. The memorial stated: "Zizong knew Pei Yan was rebelling yet said nothing."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he took Ren'gui's memorial and departed. The memorial read: "Zizong knew Pei Yan was plotting rebellion and said nothing."

sentences.zh: 」太后覽之，命拉嗣宗於殿庭，絞於都亭。

translations.literal: The empress dowager read it and ordered Zizong dragged into the palace courtyard and strangled at Duting.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager read it and ordered Zizong dragged into the palace courtyard and strangled at Duting.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，追削李敬業祖考官爵，發塚斫棺，複姓徐氏。

translations.literal: On dingyou day, Li Jingye's grandfather and father were posthumously stripped of titles and ranks; their tombs were opened, coffins broken, and the family surname restored to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day, the court posthumously stripped Li Jingye's grandfather and father of their titles, opened their graves and smashed their coffins, and restored the family surname to Xu.

sentences.zh: 李景諶罷為司賓少卿，以右史武康沈君諒、著作郎崔察為正諫大夫、同平章事。

translations.literal: Li Jingchen was dismissed as Director of the Office of Foreign Ceremonials. Right historian Shen Junliang of Wukang and Compiler Cui Cha were made Grand Remonstrance Grand Masters and Associate Directors of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingchen was removed and made Vice Director of the Office of Foreign Ceremonials. Right historian Shen Junliang of Wukang and compiler Cui Cha were appointed Grand Remonstrance Grand Masters and Associate Directors of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 徐敬業聞李孝逸將至，自潤州回軍拒之，屯高郵之下阿溪；

translations.literal: Xu Jingye, hearing that Li Xiaoyi was approaching, withdrew his army from Run Prefecture to oppose him and encamped at Xia'a Brook below Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Li Xiaoyi was approaching, Xu Jingye withdrew from Runzhou to meet him and encamped at Xia'a Brook below Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 使徐敬猷逼淮陰，別將韋超、尉遲昭屯都梁山。

translations.literal: He sent Xu Jingyou to press Huaiyin, while separate commanders Wei Chao and Yuchi Zhao encamped at Duliang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xu Jingyou to threaten Huaiyin, while his lieutenants Wei Chao and Yuchi Zhao held Duliang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 李孝逸軍至臨淮，偏將雷仁智與敬業戰，不利，孝逸懼，按兵不進。

translations.literal: When Li Xiaoyi's army reached Linhuai, his lieutenant Lei Renzhi fought Jingye with ill results. Xiaoyi grew fearful and halted his troops, not advancing.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiaoyi's army reached Linhuai, his lieutenant Lei Renzhi fought Jingye and was beaten back. Xiaoyi lost nerve and halted his advance.

sentences.zh: 監軍殿中侍御史魏元忠謂孝逸曰：「天下安危，在茲一舉。

translations.literal: Supervising commissioner, palace aide censor Wei Yuanzhong said to Xiaoyi: "The safety or peril of the realm hangs on this single stroke."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising commissioner Wei Yuanzhong, a palace aide censor, told Xiaoyi, "The fate of the realm hangs on this one stroke."

sentences.zh: 四方承平日久，忽聞狂狡，注心傾耳以俟其誅。

translations.literal: The four quarters have enjoyed peace for long; suddenly they hear of this mad villain, and with fixed attention and strained ears they await his destruction.
translations.idiomatic: The empire has known peace for years; at the first word of this mad rebel, every quarter has turned its full attention toward his destruction.

sentences.zh: 今大軍久留不進，遠近失望，萬一朝廷更命它將以代將軍，將軍何辭以逃逗撓之罪乎！

translations.literal: Now the great army lingers long without advancing; near and far grow disappointed. Should the court by any chance appoint another general to replace you, what excuse will you have to escape the crime of hesitation and delay!
translations.idiomatic: If this great army stalls here, hope will fade near and far. Should the court replace you with another commander, what defense will you offer against the charge of delay and timidity?

sentences.zh: 」孝逸乃引軍而前。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi then led his army forward.
translations.idiomatic: At that Xiaoyi led his army forward.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，馬敬臣擊斬尉遲昭於都梁山。

translations.literal: On renyin day, Ma Jingchen attacked and killed Yuchi Zhao at Duliang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day, Ma Jingchen attacked and killed Yuchi Zhao on Duliang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛亥，以左鷹揚大將軍黑齒常之為江南道大總管，討敬業。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinhai day, Left Golden Eagle Commander Heichi Changzhi was made Grand General of the Jiangnan Circuit to suppress Jingye.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinhai day, Left Golden Eagle Commander Heichi Changzhi was appointed Grand General of the Jiangnan Circuit to suppress Jingye.

sentences.zh: 韋超擁眾據都梁山，諸將皆曰：「超憑險自固，士無所施其勇，騎無所展其足；

translations.literal: Wei Chao held a host and occupied Duliang Mountain. All the generals said: "Chao relies on perilous ground to fortify himself—infantry cannot deploy their valor, cavalry cannot stretch their legs."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chao held Duliang Mountain with a large force. The generals all said, "Chao has locked himself into rugged ground—foot soldiers cannot use their strength, horsemen cannot run free."

sentences.zh: 且窮寇死戰，攻之多殺士卒，不如分兵守之，大軍直趣江都，覆其巢穴。

translations.literal: Moreover, cornered bandits fight to the death; attacking them will slaughter many soldiers. Better to detach troops to contain him while the main army drives straight for Jiangdu and overturns their nest.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered rebels will fight to the death; storming the position will cost many lives. Better to leave a detachment to contain him while the main army strikes straight for Jiangdu and destroys their base.

sentences.zh: 」支度使薛克構曰：「超雖據險，其眾非多。

translations.literal: Logistics commissioner Xue Kegou said: "Though Chao holds perilous ground, his numbers are not great."
translations.idiomatic: Logistics commissioner Xue Kegou said, "Chao may hold the heights, but his force is not large."

sentences.zh: 今多留兵則前軍勢分，少留兵則終為後患，不如先擊之，其勢必舉，舉都梁，則淮陰、高郵望風瓦解矣。

translations.literal: If we leave many troops now the vanguard's momentum splits; if we leave few, he will become a lasting scourge. Better to strike him first—his position will surely fall. Once Duliang falls, Huaiyin and Gaoyou will collapse at the mere rumor of our approach.
translations.idiomatic: Leave too many men here and the vanguard loses strength; leave too few and he becomes a lasting threat. Strike him first—Duliang will fall, and Huaiyin and Gaoyou will crumble at the news.

sentences.zh: 」魏元忠請先擊徐敬猷，諸將曰：「不如先攻敬業，敬業敗，則敬猷不戰自擒矣。

translations.literal: Wei Yuanzhong asked to strike Xu Jingyou first. The generals said: "Better first to attack Jingye—once Jingye is beaten, Jingyou will be captured without a fight."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuanzhong urged attacking Xu Jingyou first. The other generals said, "Better to strike Jingye himself—once Jingye falls, Jingyou will surrender without a fight."

sentences.zh: 若擊敬猷，則敬業引兵救之，是腹背受敵也。

translations.literal: If we attack Jingyou, Jingye will lead troops to his rescue—we will be caught between hammer and anvil.
translations.idiomatic: If we attack Jingyou, Jingye will march to his aid and we will be caught between two armies.

sentences.zh: 」元忠曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong said: "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong said, "Not so."

sentences.zh: 賊之精兵，盡在下阿，烏合而來，利在一決，萬一失利，大事去矣！

translations.literal: The rebels' elite troops are all at Xia'a, assembled in a mob—they want one decisive clash. Should we suffer defeat, the great endeavor is lost!
translations.idiomatic: The rebels' best troops are massed at Xia'a—a rabble gathered for one decisive blow. One defeat there and the whole campaign is lost!

sentences.zh: 敬猷出於博徒，不習軍事，其眾單弱，人情易搖，大軍臨之，駐馬可克。

translations.literal: Jingyou rose from the gambling halls and is untrained in warfare. His force is thin and weak, morale easily shaken—when the great army arrives, we can take him at a halt of our horses.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyou is a gambler by trade and knows nothing of war. His force is small and brittle; one push from our main army and he will break.

sentences.zh: 敬業雖欲救之，計程必不能及。

translations.literal: Though Jingye may wish to rescue him, by the count of stages he cannot arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Jingye tries to rescue him, he cannot arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 我克敬猷，乘勝而進，雖有韓、白不能當其鋒矣。

translations.literal: Once we defeat Jingyou and advance on victory's wings, not even a Han Xin or a Bai Qi could stand against our edge.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat Jingyou, press the advantage, and not even Han Xin or Bai Qi could stand in our path.

sentences.zh: 今不先取弱者而遽攻其強，非計也。

translations.literal: To skip the weak target now and rashly attack the strong—this is no strategy.
translations.idiomatic: To pass over the weak and rush at the strong is no strategy at all.

sentences.zh: 」孝逸從之，引兵擊超，超夜遁；

translations.literal: Xiaoyi assented. He led troops against Chao; Chao fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi agreed. He attacked Chao, who fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 進擊敬猷，敬猷脫身走。

translations.literal: Advancing against Jingyou, Jingyou escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on against Jingyou, who broke free and fled.

sentences.zh: 庚申，敬業勒兵阻溪拒守，後軍總管蘇孝祥夜將五千人，以小舟渡溪先擊之，兵敗，孝祥死，士卒赴溪溺死者過半。

translations.literal: On gengshen day, Jingye marshaled his troops to block the stream and hold defense. Rear army commander Su Xiaoxiang led five thousand men by night in small boats across the stream to attack first. His army was defeated; Xiaoxiang died, and more than half the soldiers drowned trying to cross the stream.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day, Jingye drew up his army behind a stream to block the advance. Rear army commander Su Xiaoxiang took five thousand men across the water by night in small boats to attack first. His force was broken; Xiaoxiang was killed, and more than half his men drowned in the stream.

sentences.zh: 左豹韜衛果毅漁陽成三朗為敬業所擒。

translations.literal: Left Leopard Bow Guard officer Chengsan Lang of Fuyang was captured by Jingye.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsan Lang of Fuyang, an officer of the Left Leopard Bow Guard, was captured by Jingye.

sentences.zh: 唐之奇紿其眾曰：「此李孝逸也！

translations.literal: Tang Zhiqi deceived the troops, saying: "This is Li Xiaoyi!"
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhiqi deceived the rebel ranks, crying, "This is Li Xiaoyi!"

sentences.zh: 」將斬之，三朗大呼曰：「我果毅成三朗，非李將軍也。

translations.literal: They were about to execute him. Chengsan Lang shouted: "I am guard officer Chengsan Lang—not General Li!"
translations.idiomatic: They were about to cut off his head when Chengsan Lang shouted, "I am guard officer Chengsan Lang—not General Li!"

sentences.zh: 官軍今大至矣，爾曹破在朝夕。

translations.literal: The imperial army has now arrived in full force—you lot will be broken within days!
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army is upon you in full strength—your defeat is only days away!

sentences.zh: 我死，妻子受榮，爾死，妻子籍沒，爾終不及我！

translations.literal: If I die, my wife and children receive honor. If you die, your wives and children will be confiscated—you can never match me!
translations.idiomatic: If I die, my wife and children will be honored. If you die, your families will be stripped of everything—you will never match me!

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之。

translations.literal: And so they executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Then they executed him.

sentences.zh: 孝逸等諸軍繼至，戰數不利。

translations.literal: The various armies under Xiaoyi arrived in succession, but battle after battle went ill.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi's armies arrived in succession, but battle after battle went against them.

sentences.zh: 孝逸懼，欲引退，魏元忠與行軍管記劉知柔言於孝逸曰：「風順荻干，此火攻之利。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi grew fearful and wished to withdraw. Wei Yuanzhong and campaign staff recorder Liu Zhirou spoke to Xiaoyi: "The wind favors us and the reeds are dry—conditions favor fire attack."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi lost heart and wanted to pull back. Wei Yuanzhong and campaign staff recorder Liu Zhirou urged him, "The wind is with us and the reeds are dry—the moment favors fire."

sentences.zh: 」固請決戰。

translations.literal: They urgently pressed for a decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed hard for a decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 敬業置陣既久，士卒多疲倦顧望，陣不能整；

translations.literal: Jingye had held his formation for a long time; many soldiers were weary and wavering, and the ranks could not hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye's men had stood in formation for hours; many were exhausted and restless, and the line would not hold.

sentences.zh: 孝逸進擊之，因風縱火，敬業大敗，斬首七千級，溺死者不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi pressed the attack and, riding the wind, set fire. Jingye suffered great defeat—seven thousand heads were taken, and those drowned were beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi pressed the attack and sent fire downwind. Jingye's army collapsed; seven thousand heads were taken, and the drowned were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 敬業等輕騎走入江都，挈妻子奔潤州，將入海奔高麗；

translations.literal: Jingye and the rest fled on light horses into Jiangdu, took their wives and children and rushed to Run Prefecture, intending to put to sea and flee to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye and his companions fled on light horses to Jiangdu, gathered their families, and raced back to Runzhou, intending to put to sea and escape to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 孝逸進屯江都，分遣諸將追之。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi advanced and encamped at Jiangdu, dispatching generals in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi advanced to Jiangdu and sent his generals in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，敬業至海陵界，阻風，其將王那相斬敬業、敬猷及駱賓王首來降。

translations.literal: On yichou day, Jingye reached the border of Hailing but was blocked by wind. His general Wang Nazxiang cut off the heads of Jingye, Jingyou, and Luo Binwang and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day, Jingye reached the border of Hailing but was stopped by contrary winds. His general Wang Nazxiang cut off the heads of Jingye, Jingyou, and Luo Binwang and came over to the imperial side.

sentences.zh: 餘黨唐之奇、魏思溫皆捕得，傳首神都，揚、潤、楚三州平。

translations.literal: The remaining ringleaders Tang Zhiqi and Wei Siwen were both captured. Their heads were sent to the Divine Capital; Yang, Run, and Chu prefectures were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining ringleaders Tang Zhiqi and Wei Siwen were both captured. Their heads were sent to the Divine Capital, and Yang, Run, and Chu prefectures were pacified.

sentences.zh: 陳岳論曰：敬業苟能用魏思溫之策，直指河、洛，專以匡復為事，縱軍敗身戮，亦忠義在焉。

translations.literal: Chen Yue's commentary: Had Jingye been able to employ Wei Siwen's strategy—driving straight for the Yellow and Luo rivers and devoting himself solely to restoration—even if his army were defeated and he himself slaughtered, loyalty and righteousness would still have stood in his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yue commented: Had Jingye taken Wei Siwen's counsel—marched straight for the Yellow and Luo, and kept restoration as his sole aim—even defeat and death would have left loyalty and righteousness on his side.

sentences.zh: 而妄希金陵王氣，是真為叛逆，不敗何待！

translations.literal: But to vainly covet the royal aura of Jinling was truly to rebel—how could he not be defeated!
translations.idiomatic: But to chase the royal aura of Jinling was true rebellion—how could he not be destroyed?

sentences.zh: 敬業之起也，名敬猷將兵五千，循江西上，略地和州。

translations.literal: When Jingye rose, he sent Jingyou at the head of five thousand troops up the river's western bank to seize territory in He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingye first rose, he sent Jingyou with five thousand men up the west bank of the river to seize territory in Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 前弘文館直學士歷陽高子貢帥鄉里數百人拒之，敬猷不能西。

translations.literal: Former Hongwen Academy direct scholar Gao Zigong of Liyang led several hundred local men to resist him, and Jingyou could not advance west.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zigong of Liyang, a former direct scholar of the Hongwen Academy, rallied several hundred local men to resist him, and Jingyou could not push west.

sentences.zh: 以功拜朝散大夫、成均助教。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Leisure and assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Leisure and assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，郭待舉罷為左庶子；

translations.literal: On dingmao day, Guo Daiju was dismissed as Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day, Guo Daiju was removed from office and made Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以鸞台侍郎韋方質為鳳閣侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Wei Fangzhi, Vice Minister of the Crane Tower, was made Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Associate Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Fangzhi, Vice Minister of the Crane Tower, was made Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Associate Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 方質，雲起之孫也。

translations.literal: Fangzhi was the grandson of Yunqi.
translations.idiomatic: Fangzhi was the grandson of Wei Yunqi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，劉景先又貶吉州員外長史，郭待舉貶岳州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Liu Jingxian was demoted again to assistant chief secretary of Jizhou; Guo Daiju was demoted to prefect of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Liu Jingxian was demoted again to assistant chief secretary of Jizhou, and Guo Daiju was demoted to prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 初，裴炎下獄，單于道安撫大使、左武衛大將軍程務挺密表申理，由是忤旨。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Pei Yan was imprisoned, the Commissioner of Pacification for the Chanyu Road and Left Martial Guard Grand General Cheng Wuting secretly memorialized in his defense, thereby offending the sovereign's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Pei Yan was imprisoned, Cheng Wuting—Commissioner of Pacification for the Chanyu Road and Left Martial Guard Grand General—had secretly memorialized in his defense, thereby offending the throne.

sentences.zh: 務挺素以唐之奇、杜求仁善，或譖之曰：「務挺與裴炎、徐敬業通謀。

translations.literal: Wuting had always been on good terms with Tang Zhiqi and Du Qiuren. Someone slandered him, saying: "Wuting was in secret league with Pei Yan and Xu Jingye."
translations.idiomatic: Wuting had long been friendly with Tang Zhiqi and Du Qiuren. Someone slandered him, saying, "Wuting was in secret league with Pei Yan and Xu Jingye."

sentences.zh: 」癸卯，遣左鷹揚將軍裴紹業即軍中斬之，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: On guimao day, Left Golden Eagle General Pei Shaoye was sent to the army camp to execute him on the spot, and his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day, Left Golden Eagle General Pei Shaoye was sent to the camp to execute him on the spot, and his property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 突厥聞務挺死，所在宴飲相慶；

translations.literal: When the Turks heard of Wuting's death, everywhere they feasted and drank to celebrate one another.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks heard that Wuting was dead, they feasted and drank in celebration wherever they were.

sentences.zh: 又為務挺立祠，每出師，必禱之。

translations.literal: They also built a shrine to Wuting; every time they marched out, they would pray to him.
translations.idiomatic: They also built shrines to Wuting and prayed to him whenever they took the field.

sentences.zh: 太后以夏州都督王方翼與務挺連職，素相親善，且廢後近屬，征下獄，流崖州而死。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, because Xia Prefecture military governor Wang Fangyi had served in succession with Wuting and had long been on friendly terms—and also because he was a close kinsman of the deposed empress—summoned him, imprisoned him, exiled him to Yazhou, and he died there.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager, noting that Xiazhou military governor Wang Fangyi had served alongside Wuting and had long been close to him—and also that he was a near kinsman of the deposed empress—summoned him, imprisoned him, exiled him to Yazhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁未朔，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dingwei, the first day of the month, amnesty was granted throughout the realm and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month—dingwei—a general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign era was changed.

sentences.zh: 太后以徐思文為忠，特免緣坐，拜司僕少卿。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, deeming Xu Siwen loyal, specially exempted him from guilt by association and appointed him Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager, judging Xu Siwen loyal, specially exempted him from guilt by association and appointed him Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「敬業改卿姓武，朕今不復奪也。

translations.literal: She said to him: "Jingye changed your surname to Wu—I shall not take it back now."
translations.idiomatic: She told him, "Jingye changed your surname to Wu—I shall not take it from you now."

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以騫味道守內史。

translations.literal: On gengxu day, Qian Weiwei was appointed to hold the office of Neishi.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day, Qian Weiwei was appointed to serve as Neishi.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，文昌左相、同鳳閣鸞台三品樂城文獻公劉仁軌薨。

translations.literal: On wuchen day, Liu Ren'gui, Duke of Lecheng, Wenxian, Left Chancellor of the Department of Literary Works and Third-Rank Associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day, Liu Ren'gui, Duke of Lecheng, posthumously styled Wenxian, Left Chancellor of the Department of Literary Works and Third-Rank Associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, died.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸未，制：「朝堂所置登聞鼓及肺石，不須防守，有撾鼓立石者，令御史受狀以聞。

translations.literal: In the second month, on guiwei day, an edict stated: "The appeal drum and grievance stone placed in the court hall need no guard. Whoever strikes the drum or stands by the stone shall have a censor receive the petition and report it upward."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guiwei day, an edict declared: "The appeal drum and grievance stone in the court hall need no guard. Anyone who strikes the drum or stands by the stone shall have a censor take the petition and report it upward."

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以春官尚書武承嗣、秋官尚書裴居道、右肅政大夫韋思謙並同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: On yisi day, Wu Chengsi, Minister of the Department of Spring Affairs; Pei Judao, Minister of the Department of Autumn Affairs; and Wei Siqian, Right Grand Master of Rectification, were all made Third-Rank Associates of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day, Wu Chengsi, Minister of the Department of Spring Affairs; Pei Judao, Minister of the Department of Autumn Affairs; and Wei Siqian, Right Grand Master of Rectification, were all appointed Third-Rank Associates of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 突厥阿史那骨篤祿等數寇邊；

translations.literal: The Turks Ashina Gudulu and others repeatedly raided the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks, led by Ashina Gudulu, repeatedly raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 以左玉鈐衛中郎將淳於處平為陽曲道行軍總管，擊之。

translations.literal: Chunyu Chuping, middle general of the Left Jade Talisman Guard, was made campaign commander of the Yangqu Circuit to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Chuping, middle general of the Left Jade Talisman Guard, was appointed campaign commander of the Yangqu Circuit and sent to attack them.

sentences.zh: 正諫大夫、同平章事沈君諒罷。

translations.literal: Shen Junliang, Grand Master of Direct Remonstrance and Associate Director of the Chancellery, was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Junliang, Grand Master of Direct Remonstrance and Associate Director of the Chancellery, was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 三月，正諫大夫、同平章事崔察罷。

translations.literal: In the third month, Cui Cha, Grand Master of Direct Remonstrance and Associate Director of the Chancellery, was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Cui Cha, Grand Master of Direct Remonstrance and Associate Director of the Chancellery, was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，遷廬陵王於房州。

translations.literal: On bingchen day, the Prince of Luling was moved to Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day, the Prince of Luling was relocated to Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，武承嗣罷。

translations.literal: On xinyou day, Wu Chengsi was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day, Wu Chengsi was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 辛未，頒《垂拱格》。

translations.literal: On xinwei day, the Regulations of the Chuígǒng Era were promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day, the Regulations of the Chuígǒng Era were issued throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 朝士有左遷詣宰相自訴者，內史騫味道曰：「此太后處分。

translations.literal: A court official who had been demoted came to the chief minister to plead his case. Neishi Qian Weiwei said: "This was the empress dowager's decision."
translations.idiomatic: When a demoted court official came to the chief minister to plead his case, Neishi Qian Weiwei said, "This was the empress dowager's decision."

sentences.zh: 」同中書門下三品劉禕之曰：「緣坐改官，由臣下奏請。

translations.literal: Associate Director of the Chancellery Liu Yizhi said: "Demotion by guilt of association is done on memorial from subordinates."
translations.idiomatic: Associate Director of the Chancellery Liu Yizhi replied, "Demotion by guilt of association comes only on memorial from subordinates."

sentences.zh: 」太后聞之，夏，四月，丙子，貶味道為青州刺史，加禕之太中大夫。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager heard of this, in summer, in the fourth month, on bingzi day, Weiwei was demoted to prefect of Qingzhou and Yizhi was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Provision.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager heard of this, in summer, in the fourth month, on bingzi day, she demoted Weiwei to prefect of Qingzhou and promoted Yizhi to Grand Master of Palace Provision.

sentences.zh: 謂侍臣曰：「君臣同體，豈得歸惡於君，引善自取乎！

translations.literal: She said to the attending ministers: "Ruler and minister share one body—how can you shift blame onto your sovereign and keep credit for yourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: She told the attending ministers, "Ruler and minister share one body—how dare you shift blame onto your sovereign and keep the credit for yourselves!"

sentences.zh: 癸未，突厥寇代州；

translations.literal: On guiwei day, the Turks raided Dai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day, the Turks attacked Dai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淳於處平引兵救之，至忻州，為突厥所敗，死者五千餘人。

translations.literal: Chunyu Chuping led troops to rescue it, but when he reached Xin Prefecture he was defeated by the Turks; more than five thousand men died.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Chuping marched to relieve the prefecture, but at Xin Prefecture the Turks broke his army; more than five thousand men were killed.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙午，以裴居道為內史。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on bingwu day, Pei Judao was made Neishi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingwu day, Pei Judao was appointed Neishi.

sentences.zh: 納言王德真流象州。

translations.literal: Edict Officer Wang Dezhen was exiled to Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Edict Officer Wang Dezhen was banished to Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以冬官尚書蘇良嗣為納言。

translations.literal: On jiyou day, Su Liangsi, Minister of the Department of Winter Affairs, was made Edict Officer.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day, Su Liangsi, Minister of the Department of Winter Affairs, was appointed Edict Officer.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，制內外九品以上及百姓，咸令自舉。

translations.literal: On renxu day, an edict ordered all officials from the ninth rank upward, inside and outside the capital, as well as common people, to be permitted self-recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day, an edict commanded that officials of the ninth rank and above throughout the realm, and common people as well, be allowed to recommend themselves for office.

sentences.zh: 壬申，韋方質同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: On renshen day, Wei Fangzhi was made Third-Rank Associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day, Wei Fangzhi was appointed Third-Rank Associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 六月，天官尚書韋待價同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Wei Daibiao, Minister of the Department of Celestial Affairs, was made Third-Rank Associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Wei Daibiao, Minister of the Department of Celestial Affairs, was appointed Third-Rank Associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 待價，萬石之兄也。

translations.literal: Daibiao was the elder brother of Wanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Daibiao was the elder brother of Wanshi.

sentences.zh: 同羅、僕固等諸部叛；

translations.literal: The Tongluo, Pugu, and other tribes rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Tongluo, Pugu, and other tribes rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 遣左豹韜衛將軍劉敬同發河西騎士出居延海以討之，同羅、僕固等皆敗散。

translations.literal: Left Leopard Bow Guard General Liu Jingtong was sent to raise cavalry from Hexi and advance beyond Juyan Lake to suppress them; the Tongluo, Pugu, and others were all defeated and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Left Leopard Bow Guard General Liu Jingtong was dispatched to raise Hexi cavalry and march beyond Juyan Lake to suppress them; the Tongluo, Pugu, and the rest were broken and scattered.

sentences.zh: 敕僑置安北都護府於同城以納降者。

translations.literal: An order established the Protectorate General to Pacify the North at Tongcheng on a provisional basis to receive those who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: An edict provisionally established the Protectorate General to Pacify the North at Tongcheng to receive the surrendering tribes.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己酉，以文昌左丞魏玄同為鸞台侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on jiyou day, Wei Xuantong, Left Assistant Director of the Department of Literary Works, was made Vice Director of the Crane Terrace and Third-Rank Associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, in the seventh month, on jiyou day, Wei Xuantong, Left Assistant Director of the Department of Literary Works, was appointed Vice Director of the Crane Terrace and Third-Rank Associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 詔自今祀天地，高祖、太宗、高宗皆配坐；

translations.literal: An edict declared that from this time onward, in sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong would all share seats as associated spirits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that henceforth, in sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong would all share seats as associated spirits.

sentences.zh: 用鳳閣舍人元萬頃等之議也。

translations.literal: This followed the proposal of Yuan Wanqing and others, secretaries of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: This followed a proposal from Yuan Wanqing and others of the Phoenix Pavilion secretariat.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁卯，廣州都督王果討反獠，平之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on dingmao day, Wang Guo, military governor of Guangzhou, suppressed rebellious Liao tribes and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingmao day, Wang Guo, military governor of Guangzhou, crushed rebellious Liao tribes and restored order.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，癸卯，命天官尚書韋待價為燕然道行軍大總管，以討突厥。

translations.literal: In winter, in the eleventh month, on guimao day, Wei Daibiao, Minister of the Department of Celestial Affairs, was made grand campaign commander of the Yanran Circuit to suppress the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the eleventh month, on guimao day, Wei Daibiao, Minister of the Department of Celestial Affairs, was appointed grand campaign commander of the Yanran Circuit to campaign against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 初，西突厥興昔亡、繼往絕可汗既死，十姓無主，部落多散亡，太后乃擢興昔亡之子左豹韜衛翊府中郎將元慶為左玉鈐衛將軍，兼崑陵都護，襲興昔亡可汗押出咄陸部落。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the Western Turk khans Xingxiwang and Jiwangjue had died, the Ten Surnames were left without a ruler and many tribes scattered and perished. The empress dowager then promoted Yuanqing, son of Xingxiwang and middle general of the Left Leopard Bow Guard Auxiliary Office, to general of the Left Jade Talisman Guard and concurrent protector-general of Kunling, to succeed Xingxiwang as khan over the Yachu Duolu tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the Western Turk khans Xingxiwang and Jiwangjue had died, the Ten Surnames were left without a leader and many tribes broke apart. The empress dowager then promoted Yuanqing, son of Xingxiwang and a middle general of the Left Leopard Bow Guard Auxiliary Office, to general of the Left Jade Talisman Guard and concurrent protector-general of Kunling, charging him to succeed Xingxiwang as khan over the Yachu Duolu tribes.

sentences.zh: 麟台正字射洪陳子昂上疏，以為：「朝廷遣使巡察四方，不可任非其人，及刺史、縣令，不可不擇。

translations.literal: Chen Zi'ang of Shehong, proofreader of the Imperial Archives, submitted a memorial, stating: "When the court sends envoys to inspect the four quarters, unsuitable men must not be appointed; prefects and magistrates cannot go unchosen."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zi'ang of Shehong, proofreader of the Imperial Archives, submitted a memorial arguing that when the court dispatched envoys to inspect the realm, unsuitable men must not be entrusted with the task, and that prefects and magistrates could not be chosen carelessly.

sentences.zh: 比年百姓疲於軍旅，不可不安。

translations.literal: In recent years the people have been worn out by military campaigns—they cannot be left unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the people had been exhausted by war; they could not be left without relief.

sentences.zh: 」其略曰：「夫使不擇人，則黜陡不明，刑罰不中，朋黨者進，貞直者退；

translations.literal: Its gist read: "If envoys are not chosen with care, promotions and demotions are unclear, punishments miss their mark, faction-men advance, and the upright withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Its gist ran thus: "If envoys are not chosen with care, promotion and demotion grow arbitrary, punishments miss their mark, faction-men advance, and the upright withdraw."

sentences.zh: 徒使百姓修飾道路，送往迎來，無所益也。

translations.literal: The people are made only to repair roads and send off and welcome arrivals, to no benefit at all.
translations.idiomatic: The people are put only to repairing roads and greeting envoys coming and going, with no benefit at all.

sentences.zh: 諺曰：『欲知其人，觀其所使。

translations.literal: A proverb says: 'To know a man, observe whom he employs.'
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says, 'To know a man, look at whom he sends.'

sentences.zh: 』不可不慎也。

translations.literal: This cannot be treated carelessly.
translations.idiomatic: This cannot be treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「宰相，陛下之腹心；

translations.literal: It also said: "The chief ministers are Your Majesty's heart and mind."
translations.idiomatic: It continued: "The chief ministers are Your Majesty's heart and mind."

sentences.zh: 刺史、縣令，陛下之手足；

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates are Your Majesty's hands and feet.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates are Your Majesty's hands and feet.

sentences.zh: 未有無腹心手足而能獨理者也。

translations.literal: Never yet has anyone governed alone without heart, mind, hands, and feet.
translations.idiomatic: No ruler has ever governed alone without heart, mind, hands, and feet to serve him.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「天下有危機，禍福因之而生，機靜則有福，機動則有祝，百姓是也。

translations.literal: It also said: "The realm holds a point of crisis from which fortune and calamity arise; when the crisis is still, fortune follows; when it stirs, disaster follows—and the people are that crisis."
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "The realm rests on a point of crisis from which fortune and calamity spring; when that point is still, fortune follows; when it stirs, disaster follows—and the people are that crisis."

sentences.zh: 百姓安則樂其生，不安則輕其死，輕其死則無所不至，祆逆乘釁，天下亂矣！

translations.literal: When the people are secure they delight in life; when insecure they hold life cheap; when life is held cheap there is nothing they will not do; evil and rebellion seize the opening, and the realm falls into chaos!
translations.idiomatic: When the people are secure they delight in life; when they are not, they hold life cheap; when life is held cheap there is nothing they will not attempt; rebels seize the opening, and the realm falls into chaos!

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「隋煬帝不知天下有危機，而信貪佞之臣，冀收夷狄之利，卒以滅亡，其為殷鑒，豈不大哉！

translations.literal: It also said: "Emperor Yang of Sui did not know the realm held a point of crisis; he trusted greedy and sycophantic ministers and hoped to reap profit from the barbarians—yet in the end he was destroyed. Is not that warning vast indeed!"
translations.idiomatic: It also warned: "Emperor Yang of Sui did not see the crisis beneath his realm; he trusted greedy flatterers and hoped to profit from the barbarians—yet in the end he was destroyed. Is that not a warning vast enough!"

sentences.zh: 太后修故白馬寺，以僧懷義為寺主。

translations.literal: The empress dowager restored the old White Horse Temple and made the monk Huaiyi its abbot.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager restored the old White Horse Temple and installed the monk Huaiyi as its abbot.

sentences.zh: 懷義，鄠人，本姓馮，名小寶，賣藥洛陽市，因千金公主以進，得幸於太后；

translations.literal: Huaiyi was a man of Hu County, originally surnamed Feng and named Xiaobao; he sold medicines in the Luoyang markets and, through the Princess of Qianjin, gained access and won the empress dowager's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi was a native of Hu County, born Feng Xiaobao; he sold medicines in the Luoyang markets and, through the Princess of Qianjin, gained access to court and won the empress dowager's favor.

sentences.zh: 太后欲令出入禁中，乃度為僧，名懷義。

translations.literal: The empress dowager wished him to come and go within the inner palace, so she had him tonsured as a monk and named Huaiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing him to come and go within the inner palace, the empress dowager had him tonsured as a monk and given the religious name Huaiyi.

sentences.zh: 又以其家寒微，令與駙馬都尉薛紹合族，命紹以季父事之。

translations.literal: Because his family was poor and lowly, she had him joined to the clan of Xue Shao, Commandant of the Empress's Consorts, and ordered Shao to treat him as a paternal uncle by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Because his family was humble, she had him joined to the clan of Xue Shao, Commandant of the Empress's Consorts, and ordered Shao to treat him as a paternal uncle by marriage.

sentences.zh: 出入乘御馬，宦者十餘人侍從，士民遇之者皆奔避，有近之者，輒撾其首流血，委之而去，任其生死。

translations.literal: He went in and out riding imperial horses, with more than ten eunuchs in attendance. Officials and commoners who encountered him all fled; any who came near he would beat until their heads bled, then leave them and walk away, letting them live or die as chance would have it.
translations.idiomatic: He rode imperial horses in and out of the palace, attended by more than ten eunuchs. Officials and commoners who met him on the road fled; anyone who came too close he would beat until the head ran blood, then abandon where they lay and walk on, indifferent to whether they lived or died.

sentences.zh: 見道士則極意毆之，仍髡其發而去。

translations.literal: When he saw Daoist priests he beat them with all his force, shaved their heads, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw a Daoist priest he beat him savagely, shaved his head, and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 朝貴皆匍匐禮謁，武承嗣、武三思皆執僮僕之禮以事之，為之執轡，懷義視之若無人。

translations.literal: Court nobles all prostrated themselves to pay respects. Wu Chengsi and Wu Sansi both served him in the manner of house servants, even holding his reins; Huaiyi looked upon them as though no one were there.
translations.idiomatic: Court nobles prostrated themselves before him. Wu Chengsi and Wu Sansi both waited on him like household servants, even holding his reins; Huaiyi looked through them as though they were not there.

sentences.zh: 多聚無賴少年，度為僧，縱橫犯法，人莫敢言。

translations.literal: He gathered many idle young men, had them tonsured as monks, and let them break the law at will; no one dared speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered gangs of idle young men, had them tonsured as monks, and let them break the law at will; no one dared complain.

sentences.zh: 右台御史馮思勖屢以法繩之，懷義遇思勖於途，令從者毆之，幾死。

translations.literal: Right Censorate Investigating Censor Feng Sixu repeatedly bound him by law. Huaiyi encountered Sixu on the road and ordered his attendants to beat him; Sixu nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Right Censorate Investigating Censor Feng Sixu repeatedly tried to hold him to the law. Huaiyi met Sixu on the road and ordered his attendants to beat him nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，太后下詔復政於皇帝。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, the empress dowager issued an edict restoring government to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That spring, in the first month, the empress dowager issued an edict restoring rule to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 睿宗知太后非誠心，奉表固讓；

translations.literal: Ruizong knew the empress dowager was not sincere and submitted a memorial firmly declining.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong knew the empress dowager's offer was not sincere and submitted a memorial firmly declining the throne.

sentences.zh: 太后復臨朝稱制。

translations.literal: The empress dowager again held court and exercised regency.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager again held court and resumed regency.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，赦天下。

translations.literal: On xinyou day, amnesty was granted throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day of the month, xinwei, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first day (xinwei), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 右衛大將軍李孝逸既克徐敬業，聲望甚重；

translations.literal: Li Xiaoyi, grand general of the Right Guard, having defeated Xu Jingye, enjoyed very great prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaoyi, grand general of the Right Guard, had crushed Xu Jingye and now stood very high in public esteem.

sentences.zh: 武承嗣等惡之，數譖於太后，左遷施州刺史。

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi and the others hated him and repeatedly slandered him to the empress dowager; he was demoted to prefect of Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi and his faction resented him and repeatedly slandered him to the empress dowager until he was demoted to prefect of Shi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊申，太后命鑄銅為匭，置之朝堂，以受天下表疏銘。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wushen day, the empress dowager ordered bronze boxes cast and placed in the court hall to receive memorials and reports from throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wushen day, the empress dowager ordered bronze complaint boxes cast and placed in the court hall to receive petitions from throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 其東曰「延恩」，獻賦頌、求仕進者投之；

translations.literal: That on the east was called "Extended Grace"; those offering rhapsodies and encomia or seeking advancement were to submit there.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern box was called "Extended Grace"; those offering rhapsodies and encomia or seeking office were to drop their submissions there.

sentences.zh: 南曰：「招諫」，言朝政得失者投之；

translations.literal: That on the south was called "Summoning Remonstrance"; those speaking of the gains and losses of court governance were to submit there.
translations.idiomatic: The southern box was called "Summoning Remonstrance"; those commenting on the rights and wrongs of court policy were to submit there.

sentences.zh: 西曰：「伸冤」，有冤抑者投之；

translations.literal: That on the west was called "Redress of Wrongs"; those suffering wrongful oppression were to submit there.
translations.idiomatic: The western box was called "Redress of Wrongs"; those suffering wrongful oppression were to submit there.

sentences.zh: 北曰：「通玄」，言天象災變及軍機秘計者投之。

translations.literal: That on the north was called "Communication with the Mysterious"; those reporting celestial signs, disasters, and secret military plans were to submit there.
translations.idiomatic: The northern box was called "Communication with the Mysterious"; those reporting celestial omens, disasters, and secret military intelligence were to submit there.

sentences.zh: 命正諫、補闕、拾遺一人掌之，先責識官，乃聽投表疏。

translations.literal: One remonstrance official, one supplementer, and one admonisher were ordered to oversee them; the responsible official had first to be identified before memorials could be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: A remonstrance official, supplementer, and admonisher were each assigned to oversee one box; the responsible official had to be identified before any submission could be accepted.

sentences.zh: 徐敬業之反也，侍御史魚承曄之子保家教敬業作刀車及弩，敬業敗，僅得免。

translations.literal: When Xu Jingye rebelled, Baojia, son of Palace Censor Yu Chengye, had taught Jingye to make blade-chariots and crossbows. When Jingye was defeated, Baojia barely escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Jingye rebelled, Baojia, son of Palace Censor Yu Chengye, had taught Jingye to build blade-chariots and crossbows. When Jingye fell, Baojia barely escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 太后欲周知人間事，保家上書，請鑄銅為匭以受天下密奏。
