translations.literal: The empress dowager wished to know thoroughly the affairs of the world. Baojia submitted a memorial asking that bronze boxes be cast to receive secret reports from throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager wished to know everything happening in the realm. Baojia submitted a memorial proposing bronze boxes to receive secret reports from throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 其器共為一室，中有四隔，上各有竅，以受表疏。

translations.literal: The device was one chamber with four compartments, each with an opening above to receive memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The device was a single chamber divided into four compartments, each with an opening above to receive submissions.

sentences.zh: 可入不可出。

translations.literal: Items could enter but not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Submissions could go in but not come back out.

sentences.zh: 太后善之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其怨家投匭告保家為敬業作兵器，殺傷官軍甚眾，遂伏誅。

translations.literal: Before long, an enemy of his submitted to the box accusing Baojia of making weapons for Jingye and killing and wounding very many government troops; he was then executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, an enemy of his dropped a complaint into the box accusing Baojia of making weapons for Jingye and killing many government troops; Baojia was executed.

sentences.zh: 太后自徐敬業之反，疑天下人多圖己，又自以久專國事，且內行不正，知宗室大臣怨望，心不服，欲大誅殺以威之。

translations.literal: Since Xu Jingye's rebellion, the empress dowager had suspected that many throughout the realm plotted against her. She also knew she had long monopolized state affairs, that her private conduct was not upright, and that imperial clansmen and great ministers resented her and were disloyal at heart; she wished to kill on a great scale to overawe them.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xu Jingye's rebellion, the empress dowager had suspected that much of the realm plotted against her. She knew she had held power too long, that her private conduct was not upright, and that imperial clansmen and great ministers resented her in their hearts; she meant to kill on a vast scale and terrify them into submission.

sentences.zh: 乃盛開告密之門，有告密者，臣下不得問，皆給驛馬，供五品食，使詣行在。

translations.literal: She therefore threw wide the gate of secret denunciation. When there was an informer, subordinates might not question the case; all were given relay horses, supplied with food of the fifth rank, and sent to the temporary court.
translations.idiomatic: She therefore threw wide the gate of secret denunciation. Informers could not be questioned by officials; each was given relay horses, fed at fifth-rank table, and sent straight to the empress dowager's presence.

sentences.zh: 雖農夫樵人，皆得召見，廩於客館，所言或稱旨，則不次除官，無實者不問。

translations.literal: Even farmers and woodcutters could be summoned for audience, lodged in guesthouses, and if what they said pleased her, promoted out of turn to office; if there was no substance, no inquiry was made.
translations.idiomatic: Even farmers and woodcutters could be summoned for audience, lodged in guesthouses, and if their words pleased her, promoted out of turn; if their accusations proved empty, no one asked.

sentences.zh: 於是四方告密者蜂起，人皆重足屏息。

translations.literal: Thereupon informers swarmed from the four quarters, and everyone walked as though on hot coals and held his breath.
translations.idiomatic: Informers swarmed from every quarter, and people walked as on hot coals, barely daring to breathe.

sentences.zh: 有胡人索元禮，知太后意，因告密召見，擢為游擊將軍，令案制獄。

translations.literal: There was a foreigner named Suo Yuanli who, knowing the empress dowager's intent, gained audience through secret denunciation, was promoted to mobile corps general, and was ordered to manage specially instituted prisons.
translations.idiomatic: A foreigner named Suo Yuanli, reading the empress dowager's intent, denounced others in secret, gained audience, was promoted to mobile corps general, and was put in charge of specially instituted prisons.

sentences.zh: 元禮性殘忍，推一人必令引數十百人，太后數召見賞賜以張其權。

translations.literal: Yuanli was cruel by nature; when he interrogated one man he always made him implicate dozens or hundreds. The empress dowager repeatedly summoned and rewarded him to magnify his power.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli was cruel by nature; interrogating one prisoner, he always forced him to implicate dozens or hundreds more. The empress dowager repeatedly summoned and rewarded him to magnify his power.

sentences.zh: 於是尚書都事長安周興、萬年人來俊臣之徒效之，紛紛繼起。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhou Xing of Chang'an, chief clerk of the Ministry of State Affairs, Lai Junchen of Wannian, and others imitated him and rose one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhou Xing of Chang'an, chief clerk of the Ministry of State Affairs, Lai Junchen of Wannian, and others copied his methods and rose one after another.

sentences.zh: 興累遷至秋官侍郎，俊臣累遷至御史中丞，相與私畜無賴數百人，專以告密為事；

translations.literal: Xing was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of the Department of Autumn Affairs; Junchen was promoted in succession to Censor-in-Chief. Together they privately kept several hundred idle men and made secret denunciation their sole business.
translations.idiomatic: Xing rose in succession to Vice Minister of the Department of Autumn Affairs; Junchen rose to Censor-in-Chief. Together they kept private gangs of several hundred idle men and made secret denunciation their trade.

sentences.zh: 欲陷一人，輒令數處俱告，事狀如一。

translations.literal: When they wished to entrap a man, they would have several places all denounce him at once, the accusations matching exactly.
translations.idiomatic: When they wished to destroy a man, they would have informers in several places accuse him at once, each report matching the others exactly.

sentences.zh: 俊臣與司刑評事洛陽萬國俊共撰《羅織經》數千言，教其徒網羅無辜，織成反狀，構造佈置，皆有支節。

translations.literal: Junchen and Wan Guojun of Luoyang, judicial reviewer of the Ministry of Justice, jointly composed the Classic of Framing in several thousand words, teaching their followers to net the innocent, weave charges of rebellion, and construct and arrange cases, each with its branches and joints.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen and Wan Guojun of Luoyang, judicial reviewer of the Ministry of Justice, jointly composed the Classic of Framing in several thousand words, teaching their followers to net the innocent, weave charges of treason, and construct cases with every branch and detail in place.

sentences.zh: 太后得告密者，輒令元禮等推之，競為訊囚酷法，作大枷，有「定百脈」、「突地吼」、「死豬愁」、「求破家」、「反是實」等名號，或以椽關手足而轉之，謂之「鳳皇曬翅」；

translations.literal: When the empress dowager received informers, she always had Yuanli and the others interrogate them, each vying in cruel methods of questioning prisoners. They made great cangues with names such as "Fixed Hundred Meridians," "Earth-Surging Roar," "Dead Pig's Grief," "Seeking Ruined House," and "Rebellion Is True"; or they bound hands and feet with rafters and turned the body, calling it "Phoenix Spreading Wings."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the empress dowager received an informer, she had Yuanli and the others interrogate the accused, each competing in cruelty. They built great cangues bearing names such as "Fixed Hundred Meridians," "Earth-Surging Roar," "Dead Pig's Grief," "Seeking a Ruined House," and "Rebellion Is True"; or they bound hands and feet with rafters and spun the body, calling it "Phoenix Spreading Wings."

sentences.zh: 或以物絆其腰，引枷向前，謂之「驢駒拔撅」；

translations.literal: Or they tripped the waist with an object and pulled the cangue forward, calling it "Donkey Foal Uprooted."
translations.idiomatic: Or they tripped the waist with a block and hauled the cangue forward, calling it "Donkey Foal Uprooted."

sentences.zh: 或使跪捧枷，累甓其上，謂之「仙人獻果」；

translations.literal: Or they made a man kneel holding the cangue while bricks were piled upon it, calling it "Immortal Presenting Fruit."
translations.idiomatic: Or they made a man kneel holding the cangue while bricks were stacked on top, calling it "Immortal Presenting Fruit."

sentences.zh: 或使立高木之上，引枷尾向後，謂之「玉女登梯」；

translations.literal: Or they made a man stand on a high beam and pulled the tail of the cangue backward, calling it "Jade Maiden Climbing the Ladder."
translations.idiomatic: Or they made a man stand on a high beam and pulled the cangue backward by its tail, calling it "Jade Maiden Climbing the Ladder."

sentences.zh: 或倒懸石縋其首，或以醋灌鼻，或以鐵圈轂其首而加楔，至有腦裂髓出者。

translations.literal: Or they hung a man upside down with a stone weight on his head, or poured vinegar into his nose, or fitted an iron ring around his head and drove in wedges, until brains split and marrow spilled out.
translations.idiomatic: Or they hung a man head-down with a stone weight on his head, poured vinegar into his nose, or clamped an iron ring around his skull and drove in wedges until brains split and marrow ran out.

sentences.zh: 每得囚，輒先陳其械具以示之，皆戰慄流汗，望風自誣。

translations.literal: Whenever they took a prisoner, they first displayed the instruments of torture; all trembled and sweated and, at the mere sight, confessed of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they took a prisoner, they first displayed the instruments of torture; men trembled and sweated and, at the mere sight, confessed to whatever was demanded.

sentences.zh: 每有赦令，俊臣輒令獄卒先殺重囚，然後宣示。

translations.literal: Whenever there was an amnesty, Junchen would have the prison guards first kill the serious prisoners and only then proclaim the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an amnesty was issued, Junchen would have his jailers kill the gravest prisoners first and only then proclaim the edict.

sentences.zh: 太后以為忠，益寵任之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager regarded this as loyalty and favored and entrusted him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager took this for loyalty and favored and entrusted him all the more.

sentences.zh: 中外畏此數人，甚於虎狼。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court, people feared these several men more than tigers and wolves.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the court, people feared these men more than tigers and wolves.

sentences.zh: 麟台正字陳子昂上疏，以為：「執事者疾徐敬業首亂唱禍，將息奸源，究其黨與，遂使陛下大開詔獄，重設嚴刑，有跡涉嫌疑，辭相逮引，莫不窮捕考按。

translations.literal: Chen Zi'ang, proofreader of the Imperial Archives, submitted a memorial, stating: "Those in charge, hating that Xu Jingye was first to rebel and raise calamity and wishing to still the source of treachery and pursue his partisans, have caused Your Majesty to open edict prisons on a great scale and reestablish harsh punishments. Anyone whose traces touch suspicion, whose words implicate others in succession, is hunted down without exception and exhaustively examined."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zi'ang, proofreader of the Imperial Archives, submitted a memorial arguing that those in charge, furious that Xu Jingye had been first to rebel and raise calamity and eager to still the source of treachery and pursue his partisans, had caused the throne to open edict prisons on a vast scale and restore harsh punishments, so that anyone remotely suspected, or implicated by another's words under torture, was hunted down and exhaustively examined.

sentences.zh: 至有奸人熒惑，乘險相誣，糾告疑似，冀圖爵賞，恐非伐罪吊人之意也。

translations.literal: There are even wicked men who delude others, seize the moment to accuse one another, and bring denunciations on mere suspicion, hoping for rank and reward—this, I fear, is not the intent of punishing crime and comforting the people.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked men now delude and deceive, seize the moment to accuse one another, and lodge denunciations on mere suspicion, hoping for rank and reward—this, I fear, is not what it means to punish crime and comfort the people.

sentences.zh: 臣竊觀當今天下，百姓思安久矣，故揚州構逆，殆有五旬，而海內晏然，纖塵不動，陛下不務玄默以救疲人，而反任威刑以失其望，臣愚闇昧，竊有大惑。

translations.literal: Your servant has privately observed that in the realm today the people have long desired peace. When Yangzhou raised rebellion, it lasted nearly fifty days, yet within the seas all was tranquil and not a speck stirred. Your Majesty does not pursue quiet depth to rescue the weary people, but instead relies on harsh punishments and loses their hope. Your servant is dull and ignorant, yet privately holds great confusion.
translations.idiomatic: I have watched the realm and seen that the people have long yearned for peace. When Yangzhou rebelled, the revolt lasted nearly fifty days, yet the empire remained tranquil—not a ripple stirred. Your Majesty does not pursue quiet governance to rescue a weary people, but instead relies on harsh punishment and forfeits their hope. I am dull and unworthy, yet I am deeply perplexed.

sentences.zh: 伏見諸方告密，囚累百千輩，乃其究竟，百無一實。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed secret denunciations from all quarters; prisoners accumulate by the hundreds and thousands, yet in the end not one case in a hundred proves true.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen secret denunciations pour in from every quarter; prisoners accumulate by the hundreds and thousands, yet in the end scarcely one case in a hundred proves true.

sentences.zh: 陛下仁恕，又屈法容之，遂使奸惡之黨快意相仇，睚眥之嫌即稱有密，一人被訟，百人滿獄，使者推捕，冠蓋如市。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is benevolent and forgiving, yet you bend the law to tolerate them, so that wicked factions take satisfaction in mutual revenge; the slightest grudge is proclaimed as secret intelligence; when one man is accused, a hundred fill the prisons; envoys press the hunt, and officials' carriages crowd the streets like a market.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is merciful, yet you bend the law to indulge informers. Wicked men now settle scores with relish; the smallest slight is reported as treason. One accusation fills the prisons with a hundred victims; arresting envoys choke the roads like a marketplace.

sentences.zh: 或謂陛下愛一人而害百人，天下喁喁，莫知寧所。

translations.literal: Some say Your Majesty loves one man and harms a hundred; the realm murmurs and none know where to find peace.
translations.idiomatic: People say you spare one informer and ruin a hundred innocents. The realm murmurs; no one knows peace.

sentences.zh: 臣聞隋之末代，天下猶平，楊玄感作亂，不逾月而敗。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that at the end of Sui the realm was still at peace; when Yang Xuangan rebelled, he was defeated in less than a month.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Sui the realm was still at peace. Yang Xuangan's rebellion collapsed within a month.

sentences.zh: 天下之弊，未至土崩，蒸人之心，猶望樂業。

translations.literal: The realm's ills had not yet reached total collapse; the common people still hoped to live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: The empire had not yet fallen apart; ordinary people still hoped to live in peace.

sentences.zh: 煬帝不悟，遂使兵部尚書樊子蓋專行屠戮，大窮黨與，海內豪士，無不罹殃；

translations.literal: Emperor Yang did not understand and sent Fan Zigai, Minister of War, to carry out slaughter exclusively, pursuing the factions to the utmost; eminent men throughout the realm none escaped calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang failed to see it. He put Fan Zigai, minister of war, in charge of a slaughter that hunted down every associate. Not one eminent man in the realm escaped.

sentences.zh: 遂至殺人如麻，流血成澤，天下靡然，始思為亂，於是雄傑並起而隋族亡矣。

translations.literal: It reached the point of killing men like hemp and blood forming marshes; the realm was swept along and men first thought of rebellion; then heroes rose together and the house of Sui perished.
translations.idiomatic: Men were killed like hemp stalks; blood pooled into marshes. The whole realm turned restless, men turned to rebellion, heroes rose on every side, and the Sui house was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 夫大獄一起，不能無濫，冤人吁嗟，感傷和氣，群生癘疫，水旱隨之。

translations.literal: When great prisons are raised, there cannot but be abuse; the wronged lament and injure the harmonious qi; epidemics afflict the living and flood and drought follow.
translations.idiomatic: Great purges cannot avoid abuse. The wronged groan and disturb heaven's harmony; plagues follow, then flood and drought.

sentences.zh: 人既失業，則禍亂之心怵然而生矣。

translations.literal: When men lose their livelihoods, the heart of calamity and disorder is suddenly born.
translations.idiomatic: When people lose their livelihoods, the will to rebel awakens at once.

sentences.zh: 古者明王重慎刑法，蓋懼此也。

translations.literal: In antiquity enlightened kings were deeply cautious with punishments—because they feared this.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sage kings treated punishments with the utmost caution—because they feared exactly this.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武帝時巫蠱獄起，使太子奔走，兵交宮闕，無辜被害者以千萬數，宗廟幾覆，賴武帝得壺關三老書，廓然感悟，夷江充三族，餘獄不論，天下以安爾。

translations.literal: Formerly in Emperor Wu of Han's time the witchcraft cases arose, driving the crown prince to flight and bringing arms against the palace gates; innocents harmed numbered in the tens of thousands; the ancestral temple nearly fell; only when Emperor Wu received the letter of the old man of Huguan did he suddenly awaken, exterminate the three clans of Jiang Chong, and not pursue the remaining cases—then the realm was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Han the witchcraft terror drove the crown prince to flight and brought arms to the palace gates. Tens of thousands of innocents died; the dynasty nearly fell. Only when Wu read the old man of Huguan's letter did he wake, wipe out Jiang Chong's entire clan, and drop the remaining cases—then the realm was saved.

sentences.zh: 古人云：『前事之不忘，後事之師。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "Do not forget what went before—let it be the teacher of what comes after."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "Do not forget the past—it is the teacher of the future."

sentences.zh: 』伏願陛下念之！

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty to keep this in mind!
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to remember this!

sentences.zh: 」太后不聽。

translations.literal: The empress dowager did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，太后鑄大儀，置北闕。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, the empress dowager cast the Great Tripod of Ceremony and set it at the northern gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, in the fourth month, the empress dowager cast the Great Ceremonial Tripod and erected it at the northern gate.

sentences.zh: 以岑長倩為內史。

translations.literal: Cen Changqian was made Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Changqian was made director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛未，以蘇良嗣為左相，同鳳閣鸞台三品韋待價為右相。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day xinwei, Su Liangsi was made Left Chancellor and Wei Daizhi, Associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace of the third rank, was made Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinwei day, Su Liangsi was made left chancellor and third-rank associate Wei Daizhi was made right chancellor.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以韋思謙為納言。

translations.literal: On the day jimao Wei Siqian was made Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day Wei Siqian was made director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 蘇良嗣遇僧懷義於朝堂，懷義偃蹇不為禮；

translations.literal: Su Liangsi met the monk Huaiyi in the court hall; Huaiyi was arrogant and gave no courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Su Liangsi met the monk Huaiyi in the court hall. Huaiyi was insolent and refused to bow.

sentences.zh: 良嗣大怒，命左右捽曳，批其頰數十。

translations.literal: Liangsi was greatly angered, ordered his attendants to seize and drag him, and struck his cheeks several dozen times.
translations.idiomatic: Liangsi flew into a rage, had his men seize Huaiyi, and slapped his face dozens of times.

sentences.zh: 懷義訴於太后，太后曰：「阿師當於北門出入，南牙宰相所往來，勿犯也。

translations.literal: Huaiyi complained to the empress dowager; she said: "Master, you should enter and leave by the northern gate. The southern offices are where the chancellors come and go—do not intrude there."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi complained to the empress dowager. She told him, "Use the northern gate, Master. The southern offices are for chancellors—stay away."

sentences.zh: 太后託言懷義有巧思，故使入禁營造。

translations.literal: The empress dowager claimed Huaiyi had ingenious skill and therefore had him enter the forbidden precinct to build.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager claimed Huaiyi had a clever mind and let him into the inner palace to supervise construction.

sentences.zh: 補闕長社王求禮上表，以為：「太宗時，有羅黑黑善彈琵琶，太宗閹為給使，使教宮人。

translations.literal: Wang Qiuli of Changshe, a remonstrance official, submitted a memorial, holding that: "In Taizong's time there was Luo Heihei, skilled at the pipa; Taizong had him castrated as an attendant and set him to teach palace women."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiuli of Changshe, a remonstrance official, memorialized: "In Taizong's day Luo Heihei was famed for the pipa. Taizong had him castrated as a palace attendant to teach the women."

sentences.zh: 陛下若以懷義有巧性，欲宮中驅使者，臣請閹之，庶不亂宮闈。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty, because Huaiyi has clever talent, wishes to employ him within the palace, your servant asks that he be castrated, so that the inner quarters may not be thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty values Huaiyi's skill and wants him to serve inside the palace, I beg that you castrate him—so the inner quarters are not thrown into disorder.

sentences.zh: 」表寢不出。

translations.literal: The memorial was shelved and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was shelved and never issued.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，丁未，以西突闕繼往絕可汗之子斛瑟羅為右玉鈐衛將軍，襲繼往絕可汗押五弩失畢部落。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the ninth month, on the day dingwei, Huseluo, son of Jiwangye Qaghan of the Western Turks, was made general of the Right Jade Talisman Guard to succeed to the tribes of Jiwangye Qaghan commanding the Five Nushibi.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, in the ninth month, on dingwei day, Huseluo, son of Western Turk qaghan Jiwangye, was made general of the Right Jade Talisman Guard and given the Five Nushibi tribes of Jiwangye's line.

sentences.zh: 己巳，雍州言新豐縣東南有山踴出，改新豐為慶山縣。

translations.literal: On the day jisi Yong Prefecture reported that southeast of Xinfeng County a mountain had surged forth; Xinfeng was renamed Qingshan County.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day Yong Prefecture reported that a mountain had thrust up southeast of Xinfeng County. Xinfeng was renamed Qingshan County.

sentences.zh: 四方畢賀。

translations.literal: From all directions congratulations poured in.
translations.idiomatic: Congratulations poured in from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 江陵人俞文俊上書：「天氣不和而寒暑並，人氣不和而疣贅生，地氣不和而堆阜出。

translations.literal: Yu Wenjun of Jiangling submitted a letter: "When heavenly qi is not harmonious, cold and heat come together; when human qi is not harmonious, warts and growths appear; when earthly qi is not harmonious, mounds rise up."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenjun of Jiangling wrote: "When heaven is out of harmony, cold and heat strike together. When humanity is out of harmony, growths and tumors appear. When earth is out of harmony, mounds thrust up from the ground."

sentences.zh: 今陛下以女主處陽位，反易剛柔，故地氣塞隔而山變為災。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, a woman ruler, occupies the yang position and reverses firm and yielding—therefore earthly qi is blocked and mountains turn into calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, a woman, holds the yang position and reverses firm and yielding. Earth's qi is blocked, and mountains become omens of disaster.

sentences.zh: 陛下謂之『慶山」，臣以為非慶也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty calls it 'Auspicious Mountain'—your servant believes it is not auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty calls it 'Auspicious Mountain.' I say it is no auspice.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜側身修德以答天譴；

translations.literal: This foolish servant believes Your Majesty should turn inward and cultivate virtue to answer heaven's reproof.
translations.idiomatic: I believe Your Majesty should humble yourself and cultivate virtue to answer heaven's warning.

sentences.zh: 不然，殃禍至矣！

translations.literal: Otherwise calamity and disaster will arrive!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise disaster will surely come!

sentences.zh: 」太后怒，流於嶺外，後為六道使所殺。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was angry and exiled him beyond the ranges; later he was killed by an envoy of the six circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was furious and exiled him beyond the mountains. Later an envoy of the six circuits had him killed.

sentences.zh: 突厥入寇，左鷹揚衛大將軍黑齒常之拒之；

translations.literal: The Turks invaded; Heichi Changzhi, grand general of the Left Hawkish Yang Guard, resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: Turks raided the border. Heichi Changzhi, grand general of the Left Hawkish Yang Guard, met them.

sentences.zh: 至兩井，遇突厥三千餘人，見唐兵，皆下馬擐甲，常之以二百餘騎沖之，皆棄甲走。

translations.literal: At Liangjing he encountered more than three thousand Turks; seeing Tang troops they all dismounted and donned armor; Changzhi with a little more than two hundred horsemen charged them and all cast off armor and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Liangjing he met more than three thousand Turks. They dismounted and armored at sight of Tang troops. Changzhi charged with just over two hundred horsemen; they threw down their armor and fled.

sentences.zh: 日暮，突厥大至，常之令營中燃火，東南又有火起，虜疑有兵相應，遂夜遁。

translations.literal: At dusk the Turks came in force; Changzhi ordered fires lit in the camp, and fires also rose in the southeast; the barbarians suspected responding troops and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the main Turk force arrived. Changzhi had fires lit in camp, and more fires appeared to the southeast. The enemy suspected reinforcements and withdrew by night.

sentences.zh: 狄仁傑為寧州刺史。

translations.literal: Di Renjie was prefect of Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie served as prefect of Ning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 右台監察御史晉陵郭翰巡察隴右，所至多所按劾，入寧州境，耆老歌刺史德美者盈路；

translations.literal: Guo Han of Jinling, investigating censor of the Right Terrace, inspected Longyou; wherever he went he impeached many; entering Ning Prefecture, elders singing the prefect's virtue filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Han of Jinling, investigating censor of the Right Terrace, toured Longyou and impeached officials wherever he went. Entering Ning Prefecture he found elders lining the roads singing the prefect's praises.

sentences.zh: 翰薦之於朝，征為冬官侍郎。
